content.content: Launching skill: map-diocese

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/project-carlo/.claude/skills/map-diocese

# Mapping a whole diocese

You own the diocese until its PR is open. The rules are in `explore-diocese` and
`data/dioceses/README.md`; read both before you start. This page covers how to split the
work so it uses as little of the usage limit as it can.

## Why the work is split this way

An agent reads its whole context again on every step, so the cost of running one grows
with the square of how long it runs. Scranton, Allentown and Harrisburg each ran as six or
seven region agents of 10 to 17 parishes, all at once and all on Opus. Each cost $60 to $100,
about two-thirds of it spent re-reading contexts that had grown past 400k tokens of bulletin
text, probe output and screenshots. In Allentown, four of the six agents hit the usage
limit, and each resume rebuilt a large context.

So:

- **Bulky reading happens in short-lived contexts.** A `parish-scout` agent
  (`.claude/agents/parish-scout.md`, on Sonnet) researches about four parishes, writes their
  records and ends. The records, with their quoted evidence, are the result, so its report
  to you is a few lines.
- **Your context stays small.** Don't read bulletins, PDFs, probe output, rosters or whole
  records yourself. Work from command summaries (`todo`, `coverage`, `audit`, `validate`,
  `search`) and scout reports, filtered with `jq`. Read a record only to settle a question
  that spans batches.
- **One scout at a time.** Each scout starts from what the earlier ones learned, and the
  run never stalls at the usage limit with several half-finished agents. Run two at once
  only if the user asks for speed.
- **What scouts learn goes into files, not into your context.** The playbook is the
  diocese's `diocese.md`; reusable scripts go in the tools folder. After the diocese, lessons
  that apply everywhere go into the README, a skill or the CLI, where the next diocese gets
  them for free.

## 1. Set up

1. `pnpm diocese init <d> ...` and `pnpm diocese roster fetch <d> gcatholic`. If the
   diocese's directory runs WP Store Locator, `roster fetch <d> wpsl <URL>`. If scraping it
   takes more than reading one page, give it to a scout as a task (section 4).
2. Run `.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh` once, so scouts don't
   each install Chrome.
3. Make the scratch folders (`scratch/` is ignored by git):
   `mkdir -p scratch/map-<d>/tools scratch/map-<d>/scouts` and start
   `scratch/map-<d>/tools/README.md` with one line saying what the folder is for.
4. Read the structure: the diocese's family or cluster list, its closed-parishes page, its
   pastoral plan. Write what you find in `diocese.md` *Sources*. This is the one place you
   read source pages yourself, because the batches depend on it.
5. Copy the playbook from the dioceses already mapped: in `diocese.md`, fill in the
   *Bulletin publishers here* section that `init` put under *Sources* with what earlier
   dioceses in the same region found about the publishers likely to appear (e.g. Discover
   Mass's daily download cap, eCatholic sites behind Cloudflare). Keep it to the lines a
   scout needs.

## 2. Plan the batches

List the roster in one line per entry rather than reading the JSON:
`jq -r '.entries[] | [.id, .name, .city, .group] | @tsv' data/dioceses/<d>/rosters/<r>.json`.

Group the entries into batches of about four parishes that belong together: one town, one
family or cluster, or one shared pastor. Entries that might share a bulletin go in the same
batch, so one scout settles them. Use fewer parishes for a family with many churches or a
city centre full of closures. Write the batches to `scratch/map-<d>/batches.md`, with each
batch's roster ids, and tick them off there as they finish.

Start with a typical batch, not the hardest one, so the playbook fills up before the
difficult ones.

## 3. Run the scouts, one at a time

Start each scout with `Agent` (`subagent_type: parish-scout`), and give it:

- the diocese slug and the batch's roster entries as `<roster>:<id>`, with name and town;
- its scratch folder `scratch/map-<d>/scouts/<n>/` and the tools folder
  `scratch/map-<d>/tools/`;
- any leads from earlier batches that touch these entries.

Don't repeat what the agent definition or the skills already say.

When it finishes:

1. Check its records: `pnpm --silent diocese validate <d> | jq '.dioceses[] | {errors,
   incomplete}'`. Send any problem back to the same scout with `SendMessage`; its context
   still holds the parish.
2. Add its learnings to *Bulletin publishers here* (or *Rules settled*, for a decision),
   merged into what is there, not appended as a log.
3. Put each lead next to the batch it touches in `batches.md`, or settle it now if it
   spans batches (a merge, a church that belongs to another row).
4. Commit: `<Diocese>: batch <n> (<area>)`.

When a scout runs out of turns or hits the usage limit, resume it with `SendMessage` after
the reset instead of starting a new one. Its records are on disk either way.

## 4. Other tasks for a scout

Give a scout any job whose reading is large and whose answer is short. Say in the message
what it may write and what to report. For example:

- scraping the diocese's parish finder or Mass-times pages into a roster (`roster import`);
  report the entry count and anything odd;
- dating a closure by grepping a bulletin archive; report the date and the quote;
- linking the `coverage` entries left unmatched at the end, when there are more than a
  handful;
- the full fetch check (section 5); report only the rows that are not this week's issue.

Keep for yourself whatever spans batches or sets policy: merges across batches, rules for
the whole diocese, `diocese.md`, promotion and the PR.

## 5. Finish

1. `pnpm diocese coverage <d> --link`, then account for what is left.
2. `pnpm diocese audit <d> --fetch`: the only check that catches two rows publishing one
   bulletin. Settle each group it lists.
3. A fetch check of every row, as a scout task:
   `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome xvfb-run -a pnpm fetch:check --diocese <d>`.
   Discover Mass limits downloads per IP per day; if it refuses some rows, check those
   again once the limit resets.
4. `pnpm diocese validate <d>` and `todo <d>`. Write a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log*
   with the coverage numbers, how many scouts ran and the batch size.
5. `pnpm diocese promote <d> --dry-run`, read it, then `promote`, `uv run pytest` and the
   lint the repo runs. Commit, push and open the PR.
6. **Lessons for every diocese.** List in the PR description what a scout had to work out
   that would help in any diocese: a publisher's quirk worth a line in the README's
   *Traps*, a script every batch rewrote that belongs in the CLI. These make the next
   diocese cheaper.

# Exploring a diocese

Read `data/dioceses/README.md` before your first write. It has the rules, the file format,
the explanation standard, which sources to trust, and the traps. This page is the short
version.

To map a whole new diocese, follow the `map-diocese` skill: it splits the work into small
batches for `parish-scout` agents. This page is the method each of them follows.

## The three rules

1. **One parish row = one bulletin.** Families, clusters, canonical mergers and decrees
   don't decide rows: the bulletin does. Several canonical parishes sharing one bulletin are
   one row; family members that each publish their own are separate rows.
2. **One church row = one place with public Mass now.** Oratories, chapels, shrines and
   campus chapels count. A closed building goes in `excluded/` with `reason: closed`; an
   open place that publishes nothing goes in with `reason: no-bulletin`, never `closed`.
3. **Every call is written down for an auditor.** A record's explanation and `evidence` let
   someone a year from now re-check it in minutes: a URL, the date you read it, the exact
   words, and what you inferred rather than read. Disagreements between sources are recorded,
   not smoothed over.

## Working loop

```bash
pnpm diocese list                                     # what exists
pnpm diocese todo <d>                                 # start here if the diocese exists
pnpm diocese init <d> --name "..." --state XX --gcatholic <key>   # new diocese
pnpm diocese roster fetch <d> gcatholic               # + the diocese's own directory:
pnpm diocese roster fetch <d> wpsl <finder URL>       #   or scrape it and `roster import`
                                                      #   (eCatholic finder map: parish-site-access finder.py)
```

Then, cheapest first:

1. **Structure before parishes.** Find the diocese's family/cluster list and its bulletins
   first. Settle "one bulletin or several" per group before creating rows.
2. **Find each bulletin:** `probe url <site>` (alive? redirected? squatted? which ids does
   it embed?), `probe po <org slug | LPi id>` (a ParishesOnline org's address, ids and
   latest issues), `probe container <a/b> --pages 3` (latest masthead; `--all --step 4` for
   a monthly changelog), `probe pdf <url> --grep <name>` (any bulletin's text; date closures
   this way). When `probe url` says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no ids, the
   `parish-site-access` skill opens the site in a real browser, and it reads eCatholic and
   Discover Mass issues the way `probe container` reads ParishesOnline ones.
3. **Create records:** `pnpm diocese new parish|church|excluded|open <d> ...`. For churches,
   use `--from gcatholic:<id>` to prefill the address, Plus Code coordinates and evidence.
   **Then edit the file**: replace every TODO with the explanation, add dated `evidence` with
   verbatim `quote`s, and record `publication` ids on every parish.
4. **Before any parish row, run `pnpm diocese search <words>`.** It covers every diocese,
   the exclusions and the live CSVs.
5. **Merge rows that turn out to share a bulletin** with `pnpm diocese merge <d> <rows> --into
   <row>`. Only do it when the shared bulletin is current and each member's own old channel
   is silent. One live member channel means no merge.
6. **Account for every roster entry:** `pnpm diocese coverage <d> [--link]`. Link naming
   artefacts by adding `<roster>:<id>` to the record's `roster`, and create records for real
   gaps.
7. **Audit structure every session:** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]`. Coverage can't see
   two rows that are really one bulletin.
8. **Check the fetch:** `pnpm fetch:check --diocese <d> --parish <slug>` resolves and
   downloads a row's bulletin before it is promoted (headed: `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome
   xvfb-run -a` in the cloud sandbox).
9. **Finish:** `pnpm diocese validate <d>` (and `uv run pytest tests/test_dioceses.py`), a
   dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, commit.

A closure after the fact: `pnpm diocese exclude <d> <church> --reason closed --last-mass
<date>`, then write why in the new `excluded/` file. Something you can't settle yet goes in
`open/` (or in `revisit` / `revisit_after` on a record), with the next step and a date. A
promoted church with no current Mass found and no source saying it closed: `pnpm diocese
question <d> <church> --revisit "..."`, which takes it off the site until it is settled.
A `no_bulletin` parish is kept in the records but left off the site.

## Don't

- Don't close, merge or delete anything on the strength of a plan, a decree, an old
  directory, an account name or an absence from a list. Read the current bulletin.
- Don't set `name_verified` / `address_verified` true without two independent sources.
- Don't quote from a summarizing fetch tool. Read the page itself (`probe pdf`, `curl`); the
  quote has to be findable by `pnpm diocese recheck`.
- Don't delete a promoted record: exclude or merge it, so `promote` removes its live row.
# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
- A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo
  had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while
  St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish
  one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin
  after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7
  bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row).
- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single
  bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate.

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

**One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories,
chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a
year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building
whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said
St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday
Mass there.

**Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help`
lists them):

| reason | use it for |
|---|---|
| `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) |
| `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down |
| `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels |
| `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church |
| `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) |
| `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what |

An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If
everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`.

**Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather
than reopening them):

1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there.
   A page that merely exists is not enough.
2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church
   moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed`
   column.
3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence
   goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it.
4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its
   churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves
   them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about
   until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as
   accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a
   bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows
   were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own
   goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before.

## Files

```
data/dioceses/<diocese>/
  diocese.md            sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log
  parishes/<slug>.md    one per bulletin publisher      -> a data/parishes.csv row
  churches/<slug>.md    one per worship site            -> a data/churches.csv row
  excluded/<slug>.md    looked at and ruled out, with a reason
  open/<slug>.md        found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it
  rosters/<name>.json   outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools)
```

Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the
files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and
an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese
validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`,
`exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they
would add a validation error.

```markdown
---
name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org
bulletin_provider: parishes_online
provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202
publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091]
group: ''
evidence:
- url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf
  seen: 2026-09-25
  quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm'
  note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone.
---

## Publisher

The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline...
```

`syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight
parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into
shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess.

### Fields

Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with
`revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due.

**parish**
- `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset).
- `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`,
  `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy
  4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by
  `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/<slug>`, the church slug
  from `discovermass.com/church/<slug>/`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive`
  from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for
  `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`,
  `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page,
  or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run
  `pnpm fetch:check --diocese <d> --parish <slug>` (which reads the rows from these
  records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is
  this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README).
- `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never
  share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin
  carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form
  you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:<slug>`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are
  one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:<site id>`, `discovermass:<slug>`, or
  `url:<page>` for a self-hosted bulletin.
- `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`.
- `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and
  `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows.

**church**
- `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills
  them after promotion).
- `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`,
  `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`.
- `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the
  parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are
  others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.**
  Don't pick a favourite without saying so.
- `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `<roster>:<id>`. Written by
  `coverage --link` or by hand.

**excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`,
`decided`, `roster`.

**open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`.

**evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A
`quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck`
fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found.

## The explanation

The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file
and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check
each claim and see where your judgement came in.

**Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1)
names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be.
Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a
homepage will be different next month.

**Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five
buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak:
Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once.
When your evidence is absence, list what you checked.

**When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it,
which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next
door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was
written down.

**Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches"
is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader
needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet
confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes
after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets
done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't.

**Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer
uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/`
record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it.

The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings:

- **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites*
  (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin
  provider*, *Not yet confirmed*.
- **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement,
  coordinates).
- **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change
  this*.
- **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*.

Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote`
refuses until none are left.

A good exclusion, from Buffalo:

> **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct
> 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names
> it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday,
> November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now
> that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed".

A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in
Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later.

## Sources

Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and
how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches.
Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody
had opened.

| source | good for | lags on |
|---|---|---|
| **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** |
| The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger |
| The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages |
| The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin |
| The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass |
| Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut |
| Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened |
| GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral |
| ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members |
| OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes |
| News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover |

For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The
plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened.

## Method

Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go.

1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init <slug> --name ... --state XX --gcatholic <key>`. Fill in
   `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list.
2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch <d> gcatholic`, and the diocese's own
   directory: `roster fetch <d> wpsl <finder URL>` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise
   scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import <d> directory list.json`. Import the
   family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you
   measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese.
3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory,
   sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4)
   before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later.
4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher:
   - `pnpm diocese probe url <site>` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects,
     whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds.
   - `probe po <org slug or LPi id>` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its
     publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the
     organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container.
   - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the
     latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you
     have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left.
   - `probe pdf <url> --grep "<church or code>"` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a
     family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the
     week, then look for the issue that announces it.
   - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one
     listing per church.
5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current
   **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent,
   or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the
   ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.**
   If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's,
   so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle.
6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church <d> --parish <p> --from
   gcatholic:<id> --from directory:<id>`. This prefills the address and Plus Code
   coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the
   current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*.
7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.

**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote
<d> --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote <d>` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline
command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set:
the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until
the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes").
Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has
retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a
parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another
parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`).
Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly
run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and
`verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete
a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned.

`pnpm diocese recheck <d>` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before
promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago.

## Traps

Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once.

- **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and
  ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two
  parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the
  masthead.
- **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a
  diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin.
  `validate` rejects the truncated form.
- **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's
  bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare
  mastheads.
- **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the
  container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live.
- **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise
  the publisher just changed.
- **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A
  container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short.
- **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one
  online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the
  vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it.
- **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works.
  `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS.
- **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check
  the URL before you store it.
- **Directory street numbers are sometimes PO boxes** ("1154 Lower College Dr" was
  "PO Box 1154"), and one building can have an address on two streets.
- **A summarizing fetch tool is not a source.** For a quote, read the page itself (`probe
  pdf`, `curl`, the recheck tool). One summary moved a 2020 merger to 2026. The article's
  weekdays gave the real year.
- **A hand-written `quote:` or `note:` containing ": " breaks the YAML.** Quote the value
  (`note: 'Page 1: the masthead'`). `validate` catches it, but only after the whole file is
  unreadable, which in Albany briefly left three churches pointing at a "missing" parish.
- **Coverage measures the roster.** A place the roster doesn't list moves no number, and an
  oratory with no weekend Mass can be missing from every list and still be open. `coverage`
  lists your churches that are in no roster; each needs an explanation, not deletion.

86	# Exploring a diocese
87	
88	`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
89	out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
90	and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
91	writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.
92	
93	The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
94	is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
95	or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
96	in a few minutes.
97	
98	This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
99	churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
100	one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
101	never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.
102	
103	- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
104	- [Files](#files): layout and fields
105	- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
106	- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
107	- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
108	- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
109	- [Commands](#commands)
110	
111	## The model
112	
113	**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
114	pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
115	are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
116	decide this:
117	
118	- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
119	  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
120	- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
121	- A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo
122	  had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while
123	  St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish
124	  one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin
125	  after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7
126	  bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row).
127	- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single
128	  bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate.
129	
130	Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.
131	
132	**One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories,
133	chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a
134	year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building
135	whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said
136	St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday
137	Mass there.
138	
139	**Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help`
140	lists them):
141	
142	| reason | use it for |
143	|---|---|
144	| `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) |
145	| `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down |
146	| `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels |
147	| `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church |
148	| `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) |
149	| `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what |
150	
151	An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If
152	everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`.
153	
154	**Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather
155	than reopening them):
156	
157	1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there.
158	   A page that merely exists is not enough.
159	2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church
160	   moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed`
161	   column.
162	3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence
163	   goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it.
164	4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its
165	   churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves
166	   them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about
167	   until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as
168	   accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a
169	   bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows
170	   were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own
171	   goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before.

216	### Fields
217	
218	Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with
219	`revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due.
220	
221	**parish**
222	- `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset).
223	- `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`,
224	  `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy
225	  4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by
226	  `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/<slug>`, the church slug
227	  from `discovermass.com/church/<slug>/`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive`
228	  from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for
229	  `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`,
230	  `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page,
231	  or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run
232	  `pnpm fetch:check --diocese <d> --parish <slug>` (which reads the rows from these
233	  records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is
234	  this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README).
235	- `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never
236	  share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin
237	  carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form
238	  you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:<slug>`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are
239	  one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:<site id>`, `discovermass:<slug>`, or
240	  `url:<page>` for a self-hosted bulletin.
241	- `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`.
242	- `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and
243	  `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows.
244	
245	**church**
246	- `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills
247	  them after promotion).
248	- `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`,
249	  `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`.
250	- `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the
251	  parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are
252	  others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.**
253	  Don't pick a favourite without saying so.
254	- `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `<roster>:<id>`. Written by
255	  `coverage --link` or by hand.
256	
257	**excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`,
258	`decided`, `roster`.
259	
260	**open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`.
261	
262	**evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A
263	`quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck`
264	fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found.
265	
266	## The explanation
267	
268	The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file
269	and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check
270	each claim and see where your judgement came in.
271	
272	**Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1)
273	names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be.
274	Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a
275	homepage will be different next month.
276	
277	**Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five
278	buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak:
279	Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once.
280	When your evidence is absence, list what you checked.
281	
282	**When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it,
283	which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next
284	door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was
285	written down.
286	
287	**Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches"
288	is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader
289	needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet
290	confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes
291	after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets
292	done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't.
293	
294	**Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer
295	uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/`
296	record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it.
297	
298	The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings:
299	
300	- **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites*
301	  (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin
302	  provider*, *Not yet confirmed*.
303	- **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement,
304	  coordinates).
305	- **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change
306	  this*.
307	- **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*.
308	
309	Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote`
310	refuses until none are left.
311	
312	A good exclusion, from Buffalo:
313	
314	> **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct
315	> 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names
316	> it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday,
317	> November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now
318	> that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed".
319	
320	A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in
321	Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later.
322	
323	## Sources
324	
325	Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and
326	how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches.
327	Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody
328	had opened.
329	
330	| source | good for | lags on |
331	|---|---|---|
332	| **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** |
333	| The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger |
334	| The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages |
335	| The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin |
336	| The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass |
337	| Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut |
338	| Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened |
339	| GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral |
340	| ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members |
341	| OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes |
342	| News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover |
343	
344	For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The
345	plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened.
346	
347	## Method
348	
349	Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go.
350	
351	1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init <slug> --name ... --state XX --gcatholic <key>`. Fill in
352	   `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list.
353	2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch <d> gcatholic`, and the diocese's own
354	   directory: `roster fetch <d> wpsl <finder URL>` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise
355	   scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import <d> directory list.json`. Import the
356	   family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you
357	   measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese.
358	3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory,
359	   sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4)
360	   before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later.
361	4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher:
362	   - `pnpm diocese probe url <site>` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects,
363	     whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds.
364	   - `probe po <org slug or LPi id>` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its
365	     publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the
366	     organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container.
367	   - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the
368	     latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you
369	     have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left.
370	   - `probe pdf <url> --grep "<church or code>"` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a
371	     family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the
372	     week, then look for the issue that announces it.
373	   - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one
374	     listing per church.
375	5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current
376	   **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent,
377	   or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the
378	   ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.**
379	   If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's,
380	   so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle.
381	6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church <d> --parish <p> --from
382	   gcatholic:<id> --from directory:<id>`. This prefills the address and Plus Code
383	   coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the
384	   current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*.
385	7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage <d>` lists every roster entry that is
386	   not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches
387	   on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `<roster>:<id>` to the record's
388	   `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries
389	   to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude
390	   Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry
391	   stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones.
392	8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span
393	   several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it
394	   every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every
395	   family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one
396	   bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no
397	   coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed.
398	9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate <d>`, `pnpm diocese todo <d>`, a dated line
399	   in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit.
400	
401	**Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote
402	<d> --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote <d>` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline
403	command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set:
404	the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until
405	the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes").
406	Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has
407	retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a
408	parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another
409	parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`).
410	Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly
411	run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and
412	`verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete
413	a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned.
414	
415	`pnpm diocese recheck <d>` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before
416	promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago.
417	
418	## Traps
419	
420	Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once.
421	
422	- **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and
423	  ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two
424	  parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the
425	  masthead.
426	- **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a
427	  diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin.
428	  `validate` rejects the truncated form.
429	- **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's
430	  bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare
431	  mastheads.
432	- **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the
433	  container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live.
434	- **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise
435	  the publisher just changed.
436	- **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A
437	  container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short.
438	- **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one
439	  online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the
440	  vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it.
441	- **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works.
442	  `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS.
443	- **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check
444	  the URL before you store it.
445	- **Directory street numbers are sometimes PO boxes** ("1154 Lower College Dr" was
446	  "PO Box 1154"), and one building can have an address on two streets.
447	- **A summarizing fetch tool is not a source.** For a quote, read the page itself (`probe
448	  pdf`, `curl`, the recheck tool). One summary moved a 2020 merger to 2026. The article's
449	  weekdays gave the real year.
450	- **A hand-written `quote:` or `note:` containing ": " breaks the YAML.** Quote the value
451	  (`note: 'Page 1: the masthead'`). `validate` catches it, but only after the whole file is
452	  unreadable, which in Albany briefly left three churches pointing at a "missing" parish.
453	- **Coverage measures the roster.** A place the roster doesn't list moves no number, and an
454	  oratory with no weekend Mass can be missing from every list and still be open. `coverage`
455	  lists your churches that are in no roster; each needs an explanation, not deletion.
456	
457	## Commands
458	
459	`pnpm diocese <command> --help` gives every flag. Output is JSON (`pnpm --silent` drops pnpm's
460	banner for `jq`). Without pnpm: `uv run python -m pdf_extract diocese ...`.
461	
462	```bash
463	pnpm diocese list | show <d> | todo <d> | validate [<d>]
464	pnpm diocese init <d> --name "..." --state NY [--website URL] [--gcatholic key]
465	pnpm diocese search <words> [--diocese d|live] [--kind parish|church|excluded|open]
466	
467	pnpm diocese new parish   <d> --name ... --website ... [--bulletin-provider p --provider-id id --publication x:y --group g]
468	pnpm diocese new church   <d> --parish <p> [--from roster:id ...] [--name ... --line1 ... --city ... ...]
469	pnpm diocese new excluded <d> --reason <r> [--from roster:id] [--name ... --city ... --last-mass date]
470	pnpm diocese new open     <d> --name ... --revisit "next step" [--revisit-after date] [--from roster:id]
471	pnpm diocese merge   <d> <parish>... --into <parish> [--note "why"]
472	pnpm diocese rename  <d> <kind> <old> <new>
473	pnpm diocese exclude <d> <church> --reason <r> [--last-mass date]
474	pnpm diocese question <d> <church> --revisit "next step" [--revisit-after date]
475	
476	pnpm diocese roster fetch  <d> gcatholic [key] | wpsl <finder URL>
477	pnpm diocese roster import <d> <name> <file.json|csv> [--title --url --notes]
478	pnpm diocese roster list <d> | show <d> <roster:id>
479	pnpm diocese coverage <d> [--roster name] [--link] [--show-matched]
480	pnpm diocese audit <d> [--fetch]
481	
482	pnpm diocese probe url <url>...
483	pnpm diocese probe sites <d> [--all]
484	pnpm diocese probe po <org slug | LPi id>... [--issues N]
485	pnpm diocese probe container <a/b> [--weeks N --from date --step N --all --pages N]
486	pnpm diocese probe pdf <url> [--pages N] [--chars N] [--grep text] [--grep text2 ...]
487	pnpm diocese recheck <d> [slug ...] [--kind k] [--all]
488	
489	pnpm diocese export  <d> --out-dir DIR
490	pnpm diocese promote <d> [--dry-run]
491	```
492	
493	`validate` separates **errors** (block every write), **incomplete** (block export and
494	promote: TODOs, missing evidence, missing address, unknown provider) and **warnings**. `pytest`
495	runs it over the committed dioceses, so a bad hand edit fails CI.
496
