# Exploring a diocese `data/dioceses//` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`. The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it in a few minutes. This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151 churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both. - [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are - [Files](#files): layout and fields - [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs - [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each - [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first - [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo - [Commands](#commands) ## The model **One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is --- name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown state: PA website: https://www.dioceseaj.org status: exploring gcatholic: alto0 --- Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg), Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is where shared bulletins are likely. ## Sources Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here. - **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit, Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City; Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins. - **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary, Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin. - **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above. - **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap) mention no closures or mergers. ### Bulletin publishers here Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows otherwise. - **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. `discovermass.com/?s=` finds a church page when the parish site is blocked; St. Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church page, not a tokenised download link. - **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www./bulletins` usually opens in headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged. - **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins. The search API (`/prod/search?searchType=organization&...&latitude=&longitude=`) lists organizations near a point. - **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=`, PDFs at `pdfs//.pdf`): broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/`): a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/ `): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive. - **webparish.com/aj//** is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi, Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing to a parish's newer site: follow the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home. - **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael, Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works. - **eCatholic** here so far: St. Catherine, Duncansville (site id 37641), Cloudflare on curl, opens in headed Chrome, `fetch:check` reads it. - **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans). `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a quote, and says so. - **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a second source before verifying. - `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them. ## Rules settled for this diocese Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them. ## Log Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it. Reusable scripts for mapping the Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown (scratch, not committed).

7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `:` to the record's `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones. 8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed. 9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate `, `pnpm diocese todo `, a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit. **Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote ` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set: the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes"). Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`). Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and `verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned. `pnpm diocese recheck ` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago. ## Traps Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once. - **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the masthead. - **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin. `validate` rejects the truncated form. - **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare mastheads. - **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live. - **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise the publisher just changed. - **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short. - **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it. - **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works. `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS. - **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check the URL before you store it. - **Directory street numbers are sometimes PO boxes** ("1154 Lower College Dr" was "PO Box 1154"), and one building can have an address on two streets. - **A summarizing fetch tool is not a source.** For a quote, read the page itself (`probe pdf`, `curl`, the recheck tool). One summary moved a 2020 merger to 2026. The article's weekdays gave the real year. - **A hand-written `quote:` or `note:` containing ": " breaks the YAML.** Quote the value (`note: 'Page 1: the masthead'`). `validate` catches it, but only after the whole file is unreadable, which in Albany briefly left three churches pointing at a "missing" parish. - **Coverage measures the roster.** A place the roster doesn't list moves no number, and an oratory with no weekend Mass can be missing from every list and still be open. `coverage` lists your churches that are in no roster; each needs an explanation, not deletion. ## Commands `pnpm diocese --help` gives every flag. Output is JSON (`pnpm --silent` drops pnpm's banner for `jq`). Without pnpm: `uv run python -m pdf_extract diocese ...`. ```bash pnpm diocese list | show | todo | validate [] pnpm diocese init --name "..." --state NY [--website URL] [--gcatholic key] pnpm diocese search [--diocese d|live] [--kind parish|church|excluded|open] pnpm diocese new parish --name ... --website ... [--bulletin-provider p --provider-id id --publication x:y --group g] pnpm diocese new church --parish

---

## Publisher

St. John the Evangelist, Lakemont (Altoona) publishes its own weekly bulletin on its own
WordPress site. I rendered page 1 of the 18 October 2026 issue (the newest, 6 pages, no text
layer) on 2026-10-21. Its masthead reads "St. John the Evangelist Church, 309 Lotz Avenue,
Altoona, PA 16602" with the Mass schedule "SATURDAY - 4:00 PM, SUNDAY - 8:00 AM & 11:00 AM"
and weekday Masses, and names Monsignor Michael Becker. It mentions no other church or parish.
The diocese's directory lists the parish with one church and no companion parish, and the
directory's Mass times (Sat 4:00 PM, Sun 8:00 AM and 11:00 AM) agree with the masthead.

## Worship sites

One church, St. John the Evangelist (churches/saint-john-the-evangelist-altoona). Nothing
else is named in the masthead or the directory entry.

## Website and bulletin provider

`https://stjohnsaltoona.org/bulletins/` lists every issue as a PDF link, so the resolver reads
it as `page-pdfs` (`provider: other`). `pnpm fetch:check --diocese altoona-johnstown --parish
saint-john-the-evangelist-altoona` on 2026-10-21 picked
`https://stjohnsaltoona.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/October-18-2026.pdf` (url date
2026-10-18, 652,815 bytes, status ok), the current issue, with recipe `page-pdfs`. `provider_id` is that recipe, `page-pdfs`.

**The bulletins are image-only** (scans: `probe pdf` reports "no extractable text"), so the
pipeline has to read them as images. `recheck` cannot find quotes in them, which is why the
evidence for this issue is a note, not a quote. The directory homepage was `http://stjohnsaltoona.org/`,
which redirects to the https site; `publication` is `url:` of the bulletins page.

## Not yet confirmed

Nothing about the bulletin. The street address of the church is disputed; see the church record.

	 THE CATHOLIC COMMUNITY OF ​SAINT MARK'S AND HOLY ROSARY 
 SAINT MARK'S CATHOLIC CHURCH               HOLY ROSARY CATHOLIC CHURCH 
 ​416 Sixth Avenue, Altoona, PA 16602  TELEPHONE NUMBER:     814 942-0364 Pastor ​Father Nelson Javier T.O.R.  OUR MISSION  The parish of Saint Mark’s Roman Catholic Church is a friendly and family-oriented church.  We dedicate ourselves to proclaiming God’s Word, the dispensing of sacraments, and the building of a community of believers. We include in our mission our parish family, guests, our homes for the elderly, and our youth.  Our intention is to do what Jesus asks of his disciples in the Gospel of Saint Mark, “… ‘Go into the whole world and proclaim the gospel to every creature’.”                                                                              Mark 16:15 We emphasize Trinitarian spirituality as expressed ​in the following prayer: Father use me.  Jesus heal me.  Spirit teach me.    _____________________________________________ SAINT MARK – Patron Saint of Attorneys, Captives and Notaries – Feast Day, April 25      Saint Mark was the author of the second Gospel and a disciple of Peter.  He is said to have traveled with Peter and Barnabas, who was Mark’s cousin, on missionary work on the island of Cyprus.  He is also said to have been with Peter and Paul in Rome.  Believed to have been written in Rome sometime before the year 60 AD, the Gospel of Mark was written in Greek for the Gentile converts to Christianity.  It is widely held that the Romans requested that Mark document the teachings of Peter.  This is supported by the fact that the second Gospel is a record of the life of Jesus from the perspective of Peter.  Representations of Mark often include lions or winged lions and scrolls or books representing his Gospel.    PRAYER TO SAINT MARK O Glorious Saint Mark, through the grace of God our Father, you became a great Evangelist who preached the good news of Christ.  May you help us to know Him well so that we may faithfully live our lives as followers of Christ.  Saint Mark, we implore you to grant your special graces to our parish family.  May our parish be a shrine of peace, purity, love, labor, and faith.  Help us to share our talents, time, and treasures.  Protect and bless all of us, absent and present, living and dead.  Open our hearts to concern for others, hear our prayers, and obtain our petitions.                                            Saint Mark, Pray for Us.  =============================== 
 Pope Leo and Father Nelson, TOR -June 2025 
    ​ 900 N. Fourth Street, Altoona, PA  16601          TELEPHONE NUMBER:     814 944-6676        Pastor  ​Father Nelson Javier T.O.R. ---------------------------------------------------------- WEEKEND MASSES Saturday, Oct 17, 2026 4:30 pm Saint Mark's Church Sunday, Oct 18, 2026   8:30 am - Saint Mark’s Church    11:00 am Holy Rosary Church ========================== CONFESSIONS Saturday 12 noon - 12:30 pm Month of October Holy Rosary Church 12 noon - 12:30 pm *************************************************** SAINT MARK'S AND HOLY ROSARY 29th SUNDAY IN ORDINARY TIME October 18, 2026 TODAY’S READINGS   Our First Reading, from Isaiah, takes us back to the very foundation of our faith. In the second reading, Paul is grateful to God for the good example given by the faithful.  In the Gospel, Jesus cleverly avoids the attempt of the Pharisees to trap him on the issue of whether Jews should pay the poll tax or not.  As disciples of Christ, we should make intentional choices each day so that our lives proclaim that we indeed serve God and God alone. FALL CONFERENCE – Father Nelson will be away Monday, October 19 through Wednesday the 21st. Father Brad will celebrate morning Masses and cover for emergencies. RELIGIOUS EDUCATION Bake Sale at all masses this weekend   Thank You for your support!  First Reconciliation Session for all second-grade students and a parent on Monday, October 19, 2026, from 6-8 pm at Holy Rosary Church Hall.  This session is mandatory. YOUTH MASS  - November 1st at Holy Rosary, 11 am.       ***LAST CHANCE *** BOSCOV’S FRIENDS HELPING FRIENDS SHOPPING PASS Passes are available at all masses, either rectory or contact Sally Young.   This ONE DAY ONLY Sale is Wednesday, October 21, 2026 , 8 AM - 11 PM.  They are $5 for up to 25% Off the Lowest Sale Prices. SOUP SALE NOVEMBER 14, 2026 – The Joint Parish Social Committee are selling tickets for Chicken Noodle Soup (with roll).  Cost is $10 per quart. Pick up will be 9-11 am on Nov. 14. ​ YOUTH CHOIR PRACTICE for HOLY ROSARY 125th Anniversary Mass will be Sunday, November 1st right after the 11 am Mass at Holy Rosary Church. YOUTH GROUP ADORATION and SOCIAL every Thursday 7 – 8:30 pm Holy Rosary Grades 9-12  from Holy Rosary, St. Mark, & St. Therese   (See more details on CCD & SCHOOL Tab) SAINT JUDE TRIDUUM – Our annual Triduum to Saint Jude, Patron of those in despair or in hopeless situations, will be on Monday, October 26th, Tuesday, October 27th, Wednesday, October 28th. Mass will be at 5:30 pm each night at Saint Mark’s Church.  Candles will be lit and placed on the altar near St. Jude and Petitions will be placed in the basket also near St. Jude. The forms for Petitions and Candles will be on the back tables of both churches and inside the bulletin. A $5 donation is asked for each candle. You may put your forms in the collection baskets.  Refreshments on the last day, Wed., 28th after Mass. NEEDY ​If you are able St. Mark’s needs grocery or gas gift cards for the Needy.  Thank You! 
           F ather Nelson Javier, TOR Pastor of Saint Mark Church and Holy Rosary Church.     Thank you for being our Spiritual Leader.  God Bless You and Us.                     Emergency and Sick Calls - 814 515-9464     
 ​---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------   125TH ANNIVERSARY PRAYER WRITTEN BY BISHOP MARK L. BARTCHAK      Father of Mercy, with grateful hearts we celebrate 125 years of our Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown.  Send us your Holy Spirit to renew our hearts with the love and grace that inspired your servant, our beloved Demetrius Gallitzin, to bring the Catholic Faith to the heart of Pennsylvania.  Inspired by his apostolic zeal, help us to share the joy of being your sons and daughters.       Bless all of us on this journey of faith, which is sustained by hope and enriched by the love that you share in abundance.  We make this prayer through the intercession of Mary, Mother of the Church and Patroness of our Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown.  Amen.   ================================================================   Our Lady of the Holy Rosary, Watch Over Us; Saint Mark, Pray For Us. =================================================== CATHOLIC MINISTRIES DRIVE (CMD)- 2026  - By virtue of our Baptism, we are entrusted with gifts that are meant to be shared for the good of others.  Most of our parishioners have received the mailing to their homes. The theme this year is Sent to Serve. It is meant to tie into the history of Our Diocese and Our People and remind us that each of us has been Sent to Serve, entrusted with certain gifts meant to serve the Lord and others. Ministries within our Diocese rely on parishioner support and 100% of every donation to the CMD is directed to either the ministries funded by the CMD, or back to parishes in overages. There are envelopes on the back tables should you need one. You can either mail your donation directly to the Diocese or put it in the collection basket and mark either Saint Mark or Holy Rosary on the envelope. ========================================== Jesus, Mary, and Joseph, Pray For Us. ​==================================================================== SAINT MARK’S COOKBOOKS are available at the Rectory for $5.  They make a nice gift.  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- BLESSING HOMES – Priests can bless your home and you also can bless your own home. The family can gather at the front door and one of the family can say the following prayer:      May we who live in this home guard the sacredness of this doorway.  May God protect all who enter and leave through this doorway.  May we welcome all at this door in the name of Jesus Christ. May the blessing of God and His peace and grace rest upon all who shall pass across this threshold. Amen.   When the prayer is finished, the following mark is written above the entrance:  20 B + G + M 26 The numbers at the beginning and end stand for the year.  The letters are for the names of the Three Wisemen:  Balthasar, Gaspar, and Melchior. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- YOU  ARE IMPORTANT    - Your presence here on this website matters.  Thank you for checking in.  When we gather together for Mass, for the celebration of a sacrament, or for prayer, or here on this website, Jesus Christ is present and each of us becomes united with Christ through the power of the Holy Spirit.  Your presence makes you part of this connection which cannot be seen on the surface but is a spiritual reality that strengthens our love for one another and reminds us that we are not alone.  This is a movement of the Holy Spirit, who is constantly trying to draw us into God’s love.  You may not have noticed these little tugs before, but while you are here, we hope that you will experience that gentle pull of the Holy Spirit.  When you leave today, you will carry with you the love of Christ which has the power to instill new meaning and purpose in your life and in the lives of others.    _______________________________________________________________________ 
 ​SAINT MARK’S FACEBOOK  ­  - Shelly Frank is doing a great job maintaining a  Facebook Page  for Saint Mark’s.    The Facebook page is loaded with information and lots of pictures.  Just put the following into your search engine:   www.facebook.com/saintmarksofaltoona    - when you get there, “ Like ”  the page so that it can reach many more of our  Friends .   SAINT MARK'S WEBSITE  is maintained direct from the Rectory of Saint Mark's   We have included Holy Rosary Catholic Church on this website.    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Please see the Prayers and Spiritual Insights in the Candle Intention Section -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Please see the Bell History and Sister Elaine story in the New Section Labeled History More to Come in the New Section Liam's Journey!

content.content:
---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

## Setup, once per sandbox (~1 min)

```bash
.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh
```

This installs Google Chrome and trusts the agent proxy's TLS certificate in Chrome's store.
Before it runs, no browser starts at all:

- The venv's Playwright wants a newer Chromium than the image ships, and
  `playwright install` is blocked.
- The proxy re-terminates TLS, so every page fails with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`.

## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser

```bash
V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py"
uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org   # like probe url
uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic
uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png   # Read the PNG
```

It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered**
HTML of the page and its iframes:

- **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
  NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means
  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,
  and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF.
- **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5)
  until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no
  publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:<the page that lists them>`. That page
  may be an index linking one post per issue, or the home page itself.
- **`--follow TEXT`** clicks through to the first link whose text or href contains TEXT
  (repeatable, one URL only). The page it lands on goes under `followed`; the top-level
  fields still describe the site. Prefer a path (`/bulletins`) to a word: "bulletin" also
  matches "Publish in our Bulletin".
- **`--text` (`--chars N`), `--links` (`--match REGEX`), `--html PATH` and
  `--screenshot PATH`** read the final page. With several URLs, the file names get `-0`,
  `-1` and so on.

What it found on the 21 Syracuse sites `probe url` couldn't read (2026-09-25):

- **Behind Cloudflare:** eCatholic ids for two (`ecatholic:35905`, `ecatholic:33641`).
- **In "Bulletins" pages or widgets:** ParishesOnline ids for three (`po-org:…`, `lpi:…`,
  `po-container:…`).
- **Self-hosted:** three bulletins.
- **Dead or hijacked domains:** a parked domain, a for-sale page, and a site taken over by a
  Chinese movie-streaming page. None of these contain parish words, so they get a non-`ok`
  verdict.
- **Never loaded:** two sites stayed BLOCKED through every run (see the next section).

## When a site stays BLOCKED: find the bulletin elsewhere

Most Cloudflare sites load within a few tries, but some challenge nearly every visitor.
holyfamilyendwell.com loaded 0 times in ~25 loads over half an hour. When that happens,

Lord’s Prayer 
 
Question: 
Why don’t Catholics add the “For yours is the 
Kingdom ...” prayer at the end of the Our Father 
like Protestants do? Where did it come from? 
 
Answer: 
    The conclusion of the Lord’s Prayer that you 
refer to is called a doxology, which is a prayer of 
glory and praise. This particular doxology we do 
use in the Mass. After the Our Father, the priest 
prays the prayer that begins, “Deliver us, Lord, 
we pray, from every evil...” and the people 
respond with the doxology. The doxology is not 
found in the Bible, but it is very ancient. It was 
first found in The Didache, also called “The 
Teaching of the Twelve Apostles,” which dates 
probably from about the year AD 90. It was a 
letter of instruction to early converts to 
Christianity. Protestantism dates only to the 
sixteenth century, so the doxology is actually a 
Catholic prayer. Some scholars and the 
catechism (#2760) indicate that the doxology 
was connected to the celebration of the Eucharist 
and was not used apart from it. 
    Remember, both the Lord’s Prayer and the 
Eucharist were part of the “mysteries of faith,” 
things taught only to believers. Ironically, a 
remnant of a prayer used during the celebration 
of the Eucharist has comes to be used widely by 
many Christian churches that do not celebrate the 
Eucharist! Truth is indeed stranger than fiction!

content.content:
484:#### How the `other` resolver reads a site
485-
486-`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:
487-
488-1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
489-   (`locate.py`).
490-2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
491-   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
492-   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
493-   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
494-   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
495-   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
496-   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
497-   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs
498-   (exported as PDF), Concrete CMS and DotNetNuke (`LinkClick.aspx`) downloads
499-   as PDFs. One more collector runs only when a recipe names it:
500-   `page-images`, for a parish that posts each issue as an image (a JPEG per
501-   weekend); `fetch` stores the image as a one-page PDF.
502-3. **Choose** this week's issue among them (`choose.py`), and say why:
503-   `current` (dated this week), or a fallback (`newest-recent`, `titled`,
504-   `first-listed`). `newest-recent` is the newest issue dated in the last 45
505-   days, taken when the first listed is plainly old, or when it is neither
506-   dated nor labelled "bulletin" and the page lists a dated series.
507-
508-Each fetch result records how its bulletin was found ("page-pdfs on
509-https://…/bulletins: current"), and the run report lists any new bulletin the
510-site dated, but not this week.
511-
512-A parish can pin the first two stages with a **recipe** in its `provider_id`:
513-a collector, a bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`;
514-a collector alone reads `website` as the bulletin page). A pinned parish skips
515-the homepage and runs only its collector, so it fails loudly when its site
516-changes rather than guessing, and no change made for another site can change
517-what it picks. `fetch:check` prints the recipe that reproduces each pick it
518-guessed; pin it once the pick is right.
519-
520-When a site needs something new, add a collector rather than a branch inside
521-an existing one, and record the site (below).
522-

## Publisher

The two parishes have no separate channel, and no bulletin file at all that the pipeline
could read. Holy Rosary (900 N. Fourth St.) has no homepage in the diocese directory; the
directory gives St. Mark (416 Sixth Ave.) `churchofsaintmarks.org`, and that site is for
both: the page header reads "THE CATHOLIC COMMUNITY OF SAINT MARK'S AND HOLY ROSARY", it
gives both addresses and phone numbers, and the page says "We have included Holy Rosary
Catholic Church on this website." Both churches share Fr. Nelson Javier, T.O.R. as pastor
(the page, 21 Oct 2026; the diocese directory says the same), one weekend schedule and one
list of weekly Mass intentions ("MASSES FOR THE COMING WEEK (SM) Saint Mark Church (HR) Holy
Rosary Church", mass-information page). So this is **one row**, not two. No second channel
exists for Holy Rosary: Discover Mass has a page for each church
(`st-mark-altoona-pa`, `holy-rosary-altoona-pa`) and both say no bulletins are available.

What the site does publish is the week's notices as text on the homepage (the 18 October 2026
"29th Sunday in Ordinary Time" notices) and the Mass intentions as text on `mass-information`.
The homepage refers to "the bulletin" ("The forms ... will be on the back tables of both
churches and inside the bulletin"), so a printed bulletin exists, but I found no PDF of it:
the homepage, Mass Information, Contact Us and Archive pages (the last through headed Chrome,
because Cloudflare challenges curl on some pages) link to no PDF, widget or bulletin page.

## Worship sites

Two churches, both holding Mass now (see their records): `saint-mark-altoona` (Sat 4:30 PM,
Sun 8:30 AM, weekday Masses Monday and Friday) and `holy-rosary-altoona` (Sun 11:00 AM,
weekday Masses Tuesday and Thursday). The weekly notices also mention St. Therese's youth
group, which is a different parish (`saint-therese-of-the-child-jesus-altoona` in the
directory), not a site of this one.

## Website and bulletin provider

`no_bulletin`: the site is the parish's channel but it posts no bulletin file, so there is
nothing for `fetch` to read. `website` is the St. Mark site that serves both parishes, and
`publication` is `url:` of it. If a bulletin is ever posted as PDFs, set `other` and run
`fetch:check`. Not run now, since there is no PDF.

  Discover Mass again.
- Whether the weekly homepage notices should count as a bulletin. They are text on a Weebly
  page, not a document, so I did not treat them as one.

content.content:
# Exploring a diocese `data/dioceses//` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`. The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it in a few minutes. This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151 churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both. - [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are - [Files](#files): layout and fields - [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs - [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each - [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first - [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo - [Commands](#commands) ## The model **One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is ------ --- name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown state: PA website: https://www.dioceseaj.org status: exploring gcatholic: alto0 --- Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg), Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is where shared bulletins are likely. ## Sources Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here. - **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit, Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City; Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins. - **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary, Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin. - **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above. - **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap) mention no closures or mergers. ### Bulletin publishers here Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows otherwise. - **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21); guess the slug instead: `https://discovermass.com/church/ --pa/` on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 = not; `www.` 301s). A page can exist with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St. Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church page, not a tokenised download link. - **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www./bulletins` usually opens in headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged. - **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins. The search API (`/prod/search?searchType=organization&...&latitude=&longitude=`) lists organizations near a point. - **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=`, PDFs at `pdfs//.pdf`): broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/`): a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/ `): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive. - **webparish.com/aj//** is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi, Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing to a parish's newer site: follow the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home. - **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael, Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works. - **eCatholic** here so far: St. Catherine, Duncansville (site id 37641), Cloudflare on curl, opens in headed Chrome, `fetch:check` reads it. - **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans). `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a quote, and says so. - **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a second source before verifying. - **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/), Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date). - **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads. Cite that page directly. - `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them. ## Rules settled for this diocese Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them. ## Log Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

Expect most unmatched entries to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. "Every family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed. 9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate `, `pnpm diocese todo `, a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit. **Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote ` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set: the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes"). Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`). Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and `verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned. `pnpm diocese recheck ` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago. ## Traps Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once. - **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. - **Cathedral:** posts dated bulletins on its own site, and the weekly download check passed. Its address is disputed: the bulletin and GCatholic say 1 Cathedral Square, the diocese directory says 1405 13th Avenue.
