---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widgets, follows a site's bulletin links, and reports the same verdicts and publication ids `probe url` does, plus a `probe container` equivalent for eCatholic and Discover Mass bulletins, and a reader that turns a diocese's eCatholic parish-finder map into a roster, and a renderer for bulletin pages that are only images. Use when probe url says HTTP4XX or NO-PARISH-WORDS, or finds no publications, or when WebFetch/curl get a 403 "Just a moment..." page.
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

## Setup, once per sandbox (~1 min)

```bash
.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh
```

This installs Google Chrome and trusts the agent proxy's TLS certificate in Chrome's store.
Before it runs, no browser starts at all:

- The venv's Playwright wants a newer Chromium than the image ships, and
  `playwright install` is blocked.
- The proxy re-terminates TLS, so every page fails with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`.

## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser

```bash
V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py"
uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org   # like probe url
uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic
uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png   # Read the PNG
```

It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered**
HTML of the page and its iframes:

- **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
  NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means
  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,
  and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF.
- **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5)
  until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no
  publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:<the page that lists them>`. That page
  may be an index linking one post per issue, or the home page itself.
- **`--follow TEXT`** clicks through to the first link whose text or href contains TEXT
  (repeatable, one URL only). The page it lands on goes under `followed`; the top-level
  fields still describe the site. Prefer a path (`/bulletins`) to a word: "bulletin" also

EOF

## Publisher

No bulletin found, so `bulletin_provider: no_bulletin` (the row is kept in the records and left off
the site, README settled policy 4). St. Thomas More Parish, Roaring Spring is administered by Rev.
Allen P. Zeth, who is also Newry's administrator, but it does not share Newry's bulletin: Newry's
18 October 2026 issue (ParishesOnline 14/0551) has no Roaring Spring schedule and four 2026 issues
have no "Roaring" hit (parishes/saint-patrick-newry). One shared administrator settles one
bulletin or two only if one bulletin carries both churches, and it does not.

Channels checked on 2026-10-21, none live:

- ParishesOnline organization `st-thomas-more-church-16673`: exists, no issues.
- Discover Mass `st-thomas-more-roaring-spring-pa`: "no bulletins available".
- `webparish.com/aj/ThomasMore/`: stale diocesan stub, no bulletin.
- Guessed homepages (stthomasmoreroaringspring.org/.com, stthomasmorerspa.org, stthomasmorepa.org):
  DNS fails. `stthomasmore.org`, `stthomasmorechurch.org` and similar are other parishes.
- A Facebook page exists (facebook.com/StThomasMoreCatholicChurchPA, 168 followers) but is behind
  the login wall in the sandbox; I could not see whether it posts a bulletin.
- church-bulletin.org answers 200 for any slug with a generic landing page, so no listing there.

## Worship sites

One church, St. Thomas More (churches/st-thomas-more-roaring-spring).

## Website and bulletin provider

`website` is the old diocesan page `https://webparish.com/aj/ThomasMore/` only because the row needs
a unique URL and no live homepage exists (the directory has none). It is not a bulletin source.

## Not yet confirmed

Where, if anywhere, the bulletin is published: a Facebook post, a printed-only bulletin or one on
the Newry page. Next step: open the Facebook page in a logged-in browser or phone the parish
(814-224-4522); if a PDF turns up, change the provider and drop `no_bulletin`.

# Exploring a diocese `data/dioceses//` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`. The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it in a few minutes. This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151 churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both. - [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are - [Files](#files): layout and fields - [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs - [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each - [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first - [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo - [Commands](#commands) ## The model **One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is --- name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown state: PA website: https://www.dioceseaj.org status: exploring gcatholic: alto0 --- Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg), Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is where shared bulletins are likely. ## Sources Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here. - **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit, Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City; Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins. - **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary, Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin. - **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above. - **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap) mention no closures or mergers. ### Bulletin publishers here Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows otherwise. - **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`) list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 = not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the directory lacks. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St. Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids. - **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS, stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St. Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church page, not a tokenised download link. - **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www./bulletins` usually opens in headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged. - **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). Empty orgs: Roaring Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones. - **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph, Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin` rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages (`.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo snippet via `visit.py` reads them. - **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton; `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one. - **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale). - **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works; curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/` answers 200 with a generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing. - **WebParish still live** for St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to `webparish.com/aj//index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it. - **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18 Oct issue was not up on 21 Oct): `newest-recent` is then expected, not a fault. - **2MHost** (stjohneverettpa.org) uses ``; the fetch code honours it since batch 7. - **`probe pdf` can't take a URL with spaces**: pass `%20`. - **Nominatim** answers through the sandbox (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?street=..&city=.. &state=..&format=json`, with a user agent): use it to tell which of two GCatholic points is the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors, Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968). - **webparish.com/aj//** is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi, Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home. - **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael, Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works. - **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859), St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare 403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try, and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`). - **Self-hosted, odd hosts:** SiteGround WordPress (mhtcc.org, Huntingdon) drops `probe pdf` and plain-http curl (RemoteDisconnected or an sgcaptcha page); use https with a Chrome user agent, or `visit.py --bulletin`. Homestead (scosmu.org, Mount Union) resets https; `http://www.` works, PDFs named `_.pdf` on its About-Us page. - **findglocal.com/US///** mirrors a Facebook page's posts and Mass times without a login: useful evidence for `no_bulletin` parishes (Dudley). - **College campus Masses** (Juniata College, Tussey Hall) appear in the directory's Mass times but in no bulletin: `open/` until someone confirms they are public. - **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans). `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a quote, and says so. - **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a second source before verifying. - **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/), Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date). - **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads. Cite that page directly. - `tools/fill_record.py` fills evidence and body into a new record (see the tools README). - `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them. ## Rules settled for this diocese Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them. ## Log Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

Exit code 2

content.content:
7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `:` to the record's `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones. 8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed. 9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate `, `pnpm diocese todo `, a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit. **Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote ` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set: the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes"). Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`). Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and `verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned. `pnpm diocese recheck ` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago. ## Traps Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once. - **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the masthead. - **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin. `validate` rejects the truncated form. - **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare mastheads. - **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live. - **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise the publisher just changed. - **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short. - **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it. - **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works. `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS. - **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check the URL before you store it. - **Directory street numbers are sometimes PO boxes** ("1154 Lower College Dr" was "PO Box 1154"), and one building can have an address on two streets. - **A summarizing fetch tool is not a source.** For a quote, read the page itself (`probe pdf`, `curl`, the recheck tool). One summary moved a 2020 merger to 2026. The article's weekdays gave the real year. - **A hand-written `quote:` or `note:` containing ": " breaks the YAML.** Quote the value (`note: 'Page 1: the masthead'`). `validate` catches it, but only after the whole file is unreadable, which in Albany briefly left three churches pointing at a "missing" parish. - **Coverage measures the roster.** A place the roster doesn't list moves no number, and an oratory with no weekend Mass can be missing from every list and still be open. `coverage` lists your churches that are in no roster; each needs an explanation, not deletion. ## Commands `pnpm diocese --help` gives every flag. Output is JSON (`pnpm --silent` drops pnpm's banner for `jq`). Without pnpm: `uv run python -m pdf_extract diocese ...`. ```bash pnpm diocese list | show | todo | validate [] pnpm diocese init --name "..." --state NY [--website URL] [--gcatholic key] pnpm diocese search [--diocese d|live] [--kind parish|church|excluded|open] pnpm diocese new parish --name ... --website ... [--bulletin-provider p --provider-id id --publication x:y --group g] pnpm diocese new church --parish

[--from roster:id ...] [--name ... --line1 ... --city ... ...] pnpm diocese new excluded --reason [--from roster:id] [--name ... --city ... --last-mass date] pnpm diocese new open --name ... --revisit "next step" [--revisit-after date] [--from roster:id] pnpm diocese merge ... --into [--note "why"] pnpm diocese rename pnpm diocese exclude --reason [--last-mass date] pnpm diocese question --revisit "next step" [--revisit-after date] pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic [key] | wpsl pnpm diocese roster import [--title --url --notes] pnpm diocese roster list | show pnpm diocese coverage [--roster name] [--link] [--show-matched] pnpm diocese audit [--fetch] pnpm diocese probe url ... pnpm diocese probe sites [--all] pnpm diocese probe po ... [--issues N] pnpm diocese probe container [--weeks N --from date --step N --all --pages N] pnpm diocese probe pdf [--pages N] [--chars N] [--grep text] [--grep text2 ...] pnpm diocese recheck [slug ...] [--kind k] [--all] pnpm diocese export --out-dir DIR pnpm diocese promote [--dry-run] ``` `validate` separates **errors** (block every write), **incomplete** (block export and promote: TODOs, missing evidence, missing address, unknown provider) and **warnings**. `pytest` runs it over the committed dioceses, so a bad hand edit fails CI.  Resources Catholic Links Current News and Events Local Info The Capuchins Christian Mothers Information Select Menu Retreat Center The Retreat Center at St. John the Baptist Church Here in the mountains, enveloped by the rolling hills of the Alleghenies, surrounded by the echo of prayers and songs of the Carmelite monks who lived here for over 100 years, you will see your soul, and your life, in a new light. Built in 1890 as a Carmelite Novitiate, St. John the Baptist Retreat Center has been completely restored, with special attention to its historical value and architectural style. Its uniqueness will help make your stay with us both prayerful and Spirit-filled. That is our hope. And that has been the experience of the many hundreds who have come to experience the living God and go home renewed. Situated 30 miles above the Mason Dixon Line and 20 miles west of historic Bedford, PA, New Baltimore is within a half hour’s drive of some of the richest history to explore in Pennsylvania. Dotted with dozens of covered bridges, connected by tributaries of a hundred or more trout streams, you can walk in the same footsteps as George Washington, General Forbes, and LaFayette, from Fort Ligonier to Fort Bedford. Flight 93 is within 15 miles. Currently staffed by the Capuchin Franciscan Friars of the St. Augustine Province, individuals interested in making a retreat are also welcome. Staffed by the Capuchin Friars of the St. Augustine Province, individuals interested in making a retreat are also welcome. St. John’s Retreat Center is the perfect place! Pricing: Rooms start at $50.00 for the first night, then the price drops down to $25.00 every night after the first night. Home Cooked Meals prepared by our Staff. Per person: Cold Breakfast – $10.00 Hot Breakfast – $11.00 Lunch – $10.00 Supper – $16.00 The retreat center kitchen is available for your own food preparation if making an individual retreat. Individual Retreats – Anyone wishing to make an individual or couples retreat is welcome. Group Retreats – We have 29 bedrooms and 40 beds in all. Some rooms having two double beds. We can accomodate 40 people maximum. Discount Rates – Only for college and high school retreats Dinner Meetings – If your organization is looking for a quiet and restful place to meet and to relax, we certainly can provide a hearty meal and a quiet place to assemble. Business Retreats – It often happens that organizations that are not specifically “church related” seek a place of quiet and rest for their gatherings. Our retreat center has secure WiFi with projection for powerpoint presentations or streaming in

## Publisher

St. Catherine of Siena, Duncansville publishes its own weekly bulletin through eCatholic (site id
37641). `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:37641` on 2026-10-21 found the 18 October 2026 issue
(`files.ecatholic.com/37641/bulletins/20261018.pdf`, 2 pages, text layer readable; the 25 October
file is not up yet, 403). Page 1 is the Mass and intentions schedule for "St. Catherine of Siena
Church", page 2 the masthead "Saint Catherine of Siena Parish ... Church Address: 308 Old Route
22, Duncansville, PA 16635 ... Pastor - Reverend Jeremy J. Mohler". It names this church alone.
The diocese directory lists the parish with one church and no linked parish.

## Worship sites

One church, St. Catherine of Siena (churches/saint-catherine-of-siena-duncansville). The page 2
list of Masses is "Sunday: 5:00PM (Saturday Vigil) 8:00 AM & 11:00 AM; Daily: M-F 7:00 AM; First
Saturday: 8:30 AM", which matches the directory's times. The office is at 332 Howard Dr but holds
no Mass.

`https://www.duncansvillecatholic.org` is the eCatholic-hosted site, so `fetch` reads it from the
website (`provider_id` empty). `pnpm fetch:check --diocese altoona-johnstown --parish
saint-catherine-of-siena-duncansville` on 2026-10-21 returned status ok:
`https://files.ecatholic.com/37641/bulletins/20261018.pdf` (url date 2026-10-18, 506,527 bytes).

## Not yet confirmed

Nothing.

browser without touching the database, downloads what each one picks, and
prints one row per parish (`ok`, `resolve_failed`, `download_failed`,
`not_pdf`, or `blocked` when Cloudflare challenged the browser instead).

#### How the `other` resolver reads a site

`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
   (`locate.py`).
2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs
   (exported as PDF), Concrete CMS and DotNetNuke (`LinkClick.aspx`) downloads
   as PDFs. One more collector runs only when a recipe names it:
   `page-images`, for a parish that posts each issue as an image (a JPEG per
   weekend); `fetch` stores the image as a one-page PDF.
3. **Choose** this week's issue among them (`choose.py`), and say why:
   `current` (dated this week), or a fallback (`newest-recent`, `titled`,
   `first-listed`). `newest-recent` is the newest issue dated in the last 45
   days, taken when the first listed is plainly old, or when it is neither
   dated nor labelled "bulletin" and the page lists a dated series.

Each fetch result records how its bulletin was found ("page-pdfs on
https://…/bulletins: current"), and the run report lists any new bulletin the
site dated, but not this week.

A parish can pin the first two stages with a **recipe** in its `provider_id`:
a collector, a bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`;
a collector alone reads `website` as the bulletin page). A pinned parish skips
the homepage and runs only its collector, so it fails loudly when its site
changes rather than guessing, and no change made for another site can change
what it picks. `fetch:check` prints the recipe that reproduces each pick it
guessed; pin it once the pick is right.

When a site needs something new, add a collector rather than a branch inside
an existing one, and record the site (below).

#### Recorded sites

To keep a resolver change from fixing one site and breaking another, the pages
each resolver read on every parish's real site are recorded in
`tests/fixtures/fetch/<slug>.json.gz`, and `tests/test_fetch_replay.py` replays
them offline against the bulletin in `expected.json`, using each parish's
recipe in `data/parishes.csv` as it is now. After changing `fetch.py` or
`parish_sites/`, or pinning a recipe:

61	    text: str, reference_date: date, *, year: int | None = None,
62	) -> date | None:
63	    """A date in text. One without a year is `year`'s if given, else the nearest."""
64	    if not text:
65	        return None
66	
67	    def yearless(month: int, day: int) -> date | None:
68	        if year is not None:
69	            return safe_date(year, month, day)
70	        return _resolve_yearless_date(month=month, day=day, reference_date=reference_date)
71	
72	    normalized = _HEX_ID_RE.sub(" ", text.lower())
73	    for upload_folder in (_WORDPRESS_UPLOAD_FOLDER_RE, _WEEBLY_UPLOAD_FOLDER_RE):
74	        normalized = upload_folder.sub("/", normalized)
75	    # A file name's spaces can come URL-encoded as "+" ("10+18+26.pdf",
76	    # "August+2-+2026.pdf"): between two numbers it separates a date's parts.
77	    normalized = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)\+(?=\d)", "-", normalized).replace("+", " ")
78	    # An ordinal is a day, never a month or a year: "Oct.-4th-27th-Sun" is 4
79	    # October in the 27th week, not 27 April. Mark where one was.
80	    normalized = re.sub(r"(\d+)(st|nd|rd|th)", rf"\1{_ORDINAL}", normalized)
81	    normalized = normalized.replace(",", " ")
82	    normalized = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", normalized).strip()
83	
84	    month_name = (
85	        r"jan(?:uary)?|feb(?:ruary)?|mar(?:ch)?|apr(?:il)?|may|"
86	        r"jun(?:e)?|jul(?:y)?|aug(?:ust)?|sep(?:t)?(?:ember)?|"
87	        r"oct(?:ober)?|nov(?:ember)?|dec(?:ember)?"
88	    )
89	    # A day is never part of a longer number ("October 2026" is not October 20).
90	    # A weekend can be named by both its days before the year ("September 26 &
91	    # 27, 2026", "Oct-4-5-2025"); the year is still the issue's.
92	    # The year can also come first ("bulletin-2022-october-23"): without it,
93	    # that reads as this October 23.
94	    month_day_pattern = re.compile(
95	        rf"(?:(?<!\d)(?P<lead_year>20\d{{2}})\s+)?"
96	        rf"(?P<month>{month_name})\s+(?P<day>\d{{1,2}})(?!\d){_ORDINAL}?"
97	        rf"(?:\s*(?:&|and|-|\s)\s*\d{{1,2}}{_ORDINAL}?(?=\s+\d{{4}}(?!\d)))?"
98	        # "Bulletin_October 12_2025": an underscore can join the year on. A
99	        # longer number is no year (a mistyped "20026").
100	        rf"(?:[\s_]+(?P<year>\d{{2,4}})(?![\d{_ORDINAL}]))?",
101	        flags=re.IGNORECASE,
102	    )
103	    day_month_pattern = re.compile(
104	        rf"(?<!\d)(?P<day>\d{{1,2}}){_ORDINAL}?\s+(?P<month>{month_name})"
105	        rf"(?:\s+(?P<year>\d{{2,4}})(?![\d{_ORDINAL}]))?",
106	        flags=re.IGNORECASE,
107	    )
108	
109	    for pattern in (month_day_pattern, day_month_pattern):
110	        for match in pattern.finditer(normalized):
111	            month_num = _month_name_to_number(match.group("month"))
112	            if month_num is None:
113	                continue
114	            day = int(match.group("day"))
115	            raw_year = match.group("year") or match.groupdict().get("lead_year")
116	            if raw_year:

118	            else:

120	            if parsed is not None:

122	
123	    # Not the tail of a longer number: Weebly's "/38133239/02-12-2017" is no year 3239.
124	    for match in re.finditer(
125	        r"(?<!\d)(?P<year>\d{4})[-/.](?P<month>\d{1,2})[-/.](?P<day>\d{1,2})(?!\d)", normalized,
126	    ):

128	        if parsed is not None:

134	        normalized,
135	    ):
136	        parsed = safe_date(
137	            _normalize_year(match.group("c"), reference_date),
138	            int(match.group("a")), int(match.group("b")),
139	        )
140	        if parsed is not None:
141	            return parsed
142

144	    for match in re.finditer(

146	    ):

148	        if parsed is not None:

153	    for match in _PILOT_ISSUE_RE.finditer(normalized):
154	        parsed = safe_date(2000 + int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)), int(match.group(3)))
155	        if parsed is not None:
156	            return parsed

159	    # "20260927B.pdf". Only this century's years, so ids and timestamps don't

old='''    # Slugs and file names join words with hyphens or underscores'''
new='''    # Or as MMDDYYYY ("10112026.jpg", St. Anne, Davidsville's Wix image). Only a
    # year next to the reference date's, so an eight-digit id doesn't read as one.
    for match in re.finditer(r"(?<!\\d)(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(0[1-9]|[12]\\d|3[01])(20\\d{2})(?!\\d)", normalized):

            parsed = safe_date(match_year, month, day)
            if parsed is not None:

assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

Reusable scripts for mapping the Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown (scratch, not committed).
- `discovermass-church-urls.txt`: all 20,279 Discover Mass church page URLs (from `wp-sitemap-posts-item-1..11.xml` on discovermass.com, 2026-10-21); `grep -i <town>` finds a church's slug when `?s=` search is broken. A page's "Visit Website" link gives the parish's homepage.
- `fill_record.py <record.md> <evidence.yaml> <body.md> [key=value ...]`: replaces a freshly created record's `evidence: []` (or appends to its evidence list) with the YAML items in a file, replaces the body with a Markdown file, and sets frontmatter keys. Run with `python3 -I`. Quote any `quote:` value containing ": " yourself.

# Exploring a diocese `data/dioceses//` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`. The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it in a few minutes. This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151 churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both. - [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are - [Files](#files): layout and fields - [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs - [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each - [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first - [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo - [Commands](#commands) ## The model **One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is --- name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown state: PA website: https://www.dioceseaj.org status: exploring gcatholic: alto0 --- Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg), Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is where shared bulletins are likely. ## Sources Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here. - **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit, Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City; Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins. - **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary, Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin. - **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above. - **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21). - **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap) mention no closures or mergers. ### Bulletin publishers here Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows otherwise. - **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`) list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 = not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the directory lacks. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St. Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids. - **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS, stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St. Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church page, not a tokenised download link. - **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www./bulletins` usually opens in headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged. - **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`) lists organizations near a point. - **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly; `page-pdfs` on the site reads it. - **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=`, PDFs at `pdfs//.pdf`): broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/`): a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/ `): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive. - **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (container 14/0551). Empty orgs: Roaring Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones. - **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph, Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin` rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages (`.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo snippet via `visit.py` reads them. - **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton; `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one. - **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale). - **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works; curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/` answers 200 with a generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing. - **WebParish still live** for St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to `webparish.com/aj//index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it. - **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18 Oct issue was not up on 21 Oct): `newest-recent` is then expected, not a fault. - **2MHost** (stjohneverettpa.org) uses ``; the fetch code honours it since batch 7. - **`probe pdf` can't take a URL with spaces**: pass `%20`. - **Nominatim** answers through the sandbox (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?street=..&city=.. &state=..&format=json`, with a user agent): use it to tell which of two GCatholic points is the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors, Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968). - **webparish.com/aj//** is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi, Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home. - **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael, Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works. - **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859), St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare 403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try, and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`). - **Wix image bulletins** (St. Anne, Davidsville): one JPEG per week on the Bulletin page, alt text `MMDDYYYY.jpg`; `page-images ` reads it (the date parser takes MMDDYYYY since batch 9).
