content.content:
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `:` to the record's `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones. 8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed. 9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate `, `pnpm diocese todo `, a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit. **Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote ` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set: the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes"). Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`). Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and `verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned. `pnpm diocese recheck ` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago. ## Traps Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once. - **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the masthead. - **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin. `validate` rejects the truncated form. - **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare mastheads. - **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live. - **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise the publisher just changed. - **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short. - **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it. - **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works. `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS. - **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check the URL before you store it.

name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
  Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City;
  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.
- **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of
  them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory
  (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists
  churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John
  chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary,
  Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin.
- **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral
  plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above.
- **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org
  (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap)
  mention no closures or mergers.

### Bulletin publishers here

Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows
otherwise.

- **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken
  (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`)
  list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is
  `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 =
  not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the
  directory lacks. A joint bulletin may sit under only one of its churches' slugs (Our Lady
  Queen of Angels, Central City carries the issue for Holy Family, Hooversville and All Saints,
  Boswell, whose own pages are empty): a no-homepage parish can be a worship site of a
  neighbour's row, so read the neighbours' mastheads before calling it `no_bulletin`. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St.
  Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a
  chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids.
- **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS,
  stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and
  stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist
  with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St.
  Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several
  church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte
  "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as
  `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church
  page, not a tokenised download link.
- **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www.<domain>/bulletins` usually opens in
  headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged.
- **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins
  (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API
  (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`)
  lists organizations near a point.
- **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly;
  `page-pdfs` on the site reads it.
- **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=<id>`, PDFs at `pdfs/<id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`):
  broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/<id>`):
  a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/
  <code>`): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive.
- **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (container 14/0551). Empty orgs: Roaring
  Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones.
- **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph,
  Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin`
  rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an
  empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages
  (`<name>.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS
  (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo
  snippet via `visit.py` reads them.
- **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton;
  `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one.
- **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip
  and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale).
- **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works;
  curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/<any-slug>` answers 200 with a
  generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing.
- **WebParish is live for several parishes** (St. Thomas, Bedford; St. Anthony and St. Elizabeth
  Ann Seton, Windber, `PDFs MMDDYY.pdf` and `SEAS<YYYY-MM-DD>Bulletin.pdf`). A parish's own
  domain can redirect to its WebParish site (stelizabethannsetonwindber.com). For a parish with
  no directory homepage, a DuckDuckGo search (`uv run python visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..."`)
  finds these. Sister parishes with one pastor can each post a bulletin listing the same
  combined Mass rota (Windber): two rows while both channels are live.
- For St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to
  `webparish.com/aj/<name>/index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists
  `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it.
- **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18
  Oct issue was not up on 21 Oct): `newest-recent` is then expected, not a fault.
- **2MHost** (stjohneverettpa.org) uses `<base href>`; the fetch code honours it since batch 7.
- **`probe pdf` can't take a URL with spaces**: pass `%20`.
- **Nominatim** answers through the sandbox (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?street=..&city=..
  &state=..&format=json`, with a user agent): use it to tell which of two GCatholic points is
  the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors,
  Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968).
- **webparish.com/aj/<name>/** answers 406 (Mod_Security) to curl; headed Chrome needs the
  explicit `/index.php`. It is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi,
  Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing
  to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow
  the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home.
- **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael,
  Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every
  time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works.
- **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859),
  St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare
  403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try,
  and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:<id>` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date
  files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`).
- **Wix image bulletins** (St. Anne, Davidsville): one JPEG per week on the Bulletin page,
  alt text `MMDDYYYY.jpg`; `page-images <page>` reads it (the date parser takes MMDDYYYY since
  batch 9). St. Peter, Somerset: PHP `bulletin.php` linking `site_docs/<n>.pdf`. New Baltimore:
  WordPress, posts about a week late.
- **Partner bulletins:** in Johnstown both no-homepage parishes in batch 12 (St. Patrick; St.
  Michael) are carried in their pastor's other parish's bulletin. Read the partner's cover
  first. A parish domain redirecting to the partner's site (stpatrickjtown.com → the
  cathedral; `probe url` says REDIRECT-OFFSITE) is a fold-in, not a squat.
- **Duda** (the Johnstown cathedral, `irp.cdn-website.com`) resets curl intermittently; retry.
  Its `/welcome#WeeklyBulletin` lists `files/uploaded/YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` (not always zero-padded).
  omostoday.com (WordPress/Elementor) posts scanned issues: render with `pdftoppm`.
- **An eCatholic id on a site doesn't mean the bulletin is there**: standrewjohnstown.org is
  eCatholic (36351) but its bulletin folder is empty and its Bulletins menu goes to Discover Mass.
- **Self-hosted, odd hosts:** SiteGround WordPress (mhtcc.org, Huntingdon; stbenedictchurch.org,
  Johnstown; `tools/browser_get.py <page> <pdf> <out>` downloads a PDF through Chrome) drops `probe pdf`
  and plain-http curl (RemoteDisconnected or an sgcaptcha page); use https with a Chrome user
  agent, or `visit.py --bulletin`. Homestead (scosmu.org, Mount Union) resets https; `http://www.`
  works, PDFs named `<Month>_<D>.pdf` on its About-Us page.
- **findglocal.com/US/<town>/<id>/<page>** mirrors a Facebook page's posts and Mass times
  without a login: useful evidence for `no_bulletin` parishes (Dudley).
- **College campus Masses** (Juniata College, Tussey Hall) appear in the directory's Mass
  times but in no bulletin: `open/` until someone confirms they are public.
- **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans).
  `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a
  quote, and says so.
- **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in
  the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a
  second source before verifying.
- **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/),
  Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date).
- **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona
  cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads.
  Cite that page directly.
- `tools/fill_record.py` fills evidence and body into a new record (see the tools README).
- `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them.

## Rules settled for this diocese

Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them.

## Log

Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

content.content:
serves the same PDF from a new address each time, and some sites put each
  week's bulletin at the same one.
- `process` skips bulletins with `processed_at` already set, and serves
  bulletins it has extracted before (same PDF hash, same model) from the cache

### Checking the fetch stage

Most parishes publish through ParishesOnline, eCatholic or Discover Mass, but
the `other` provider has to find the bulletin on the parish's own website, and
every site is laid out differently. `pnpm fetch:check` runs the resolvers in the
browser without touching the database, downloads what each one picks, and
prints one row per parish (`ok`, `resolve_failed`, `download_failed`,
`not_pdf`, or `blocked` when Cloudflare challenged the browser instead).

#### How the `other` resolver reads a site

`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
   (`locate.py`).
2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs
   (exported as PDF), Concrete CMS and DotNetNuke (`LinkClick.aspx`) downloads
   as PDFs. One more collector runs only when a recipe names it:
   `page-images`, for a parish that posts each issue as an image (a JPEG per
   weekend); `fetch` stores the image as a one-page PDF.
3. **Choose** this week's issue among them (`choose.py`), and say why:
   `current` (dated this week), or a fallback (`newest-recent`, `titled`,
   `first-listed`). `newest-recent` is the newest issue dated in the last 45
   days, taken when the first listed is plainly old, or when it is neither
   dated nor labelled "bulletin" and the page lists a dated series.

Each fetch result records how its bulletin was found ("page-pdfs on
https://…/bulletins: current"), and the run report lists any new bulletin the
site dated, but not this week.

A parish can pin the first two stages with a **recipe** in its `provider_id`:
a collector, a bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`;
a collector alone reads `website` as the bulletin page). A pinned parish skips
the homepage and runs only its collector, so it fails loudly when its site
changes rather than guessing, and no change made for another site can change
what it picks. `fetch:check` prints the recipe that reproduces each pick it
guessed; pin it once the pick is right.

When a site needs something new, add a collector rather than a branch inside
an existing one, and record the site (below).

#### Recorded sites

To keep a resolver change from fixing one site and breaking another, the pages
each resolver read on every parish's real site are recorded in
`tests/fixtures/fetch/<slug>.json.gz`, and `tests/test_fetch_replay.py` replays
them offline against the bulletin in `expected.json`, using each parish's
recipe in `data/parishes.csv` as it is now. After changing `fetch.py` or
`parish_sites/`, or pinning a recipe:

1. Run `pnpm test`. A changed pick on any recorded site fails the replay test.
   A site that now opens a page the old resolver never did fails with "re-record
   this parish".
2. Re-record the sites whose result should change, then check them by hand:
   `pnpm fetch:check --parish SLUG --record tests/fixtures/fetch`.
3. Update their entries in `tests/fixtures/fetch/expected.json`. That diff is the
   coverage change.

Python 3.13.16
"""`probe url` with a real browser: see a parish website the way a person does.

`pnpm diocese probe url` fetches pages without a browser, so it reports
HTTP4XX for sites behind Cloudflare (every eCatholic site, many others),
NO-PARISH-WORDS for sites built in JavaScript (Wix, Squarespace, "Redirecting..."
shells), and no publications for bulletins that sit in an iframe widget or one
click deep. This opens the page in the pipeline's own stealth browser
(pdf_extract.browser.launch_stealth_browser) with real Chrome, headed under
xvfb, and reports the same fields `probe url` does, read from the rendered page
and its iframes. Run scripts/setup_browser.sh once per sandbox first.

Cloudflare decides per request whether to challenge, and in a Claude Code sandbox
the challenge can never be solved (brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com is denied
by the egress policy), so a challenged load is simply retried with backoff.

Usage (from the repo root; re-runs itself under xvfb-run when there is no display):
  uv run python .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py URL [URL ...] [options]

  --bulletin        when a page embeds no publication id, open its bulletin links
                    (up to 5) until one does, the way detect.py does; bulletin PDFs
                    with no publisher are reported as self-hosted (url:<page>)
  --follow TEXT     after loading, follow the first link whose text or href contains
                    TEXT (case-insensitive); repeat to walk deeper (single URL only)
  --text            include the visible text of the final page (--chars N, default 4000)
  --links           include the final page's links as [text, href] (--match REGEX filters)
  --screenshot PATH full-page screenshot of the final page (look at it with Read);
                    with several URLs, -0, -1, ... is added to the name
  --html PATH       save the final page's HTML, iframes included (numbered like --screenshot)
  --retries N       loads per navigation while Cloudflare challenges (default 8)

## Publisher

No bulletin found. Saints Gregory and Barnabas Parish (pastor Rev. Callistus Elue) has no website of its own: the directory lists none, the old ssgregbar.org does not resolve, its WebParish page (webparish.com/aj/GregoryandBarnabas) is a stub with no bulletin, its Discover Mass page (`st-gregory-johnstown-pa`) says "no bulletins available", and the ParishesOnline organizations for the parish and for St. Barnabas are empty. Its only public online presence found is a Facebook page, behind a login wall here.

Searched on 2026-10-21: `probe url` on the old and WebParish sites; `probe po` on both ParishesOnline organizations; Discover Mass for Gregory, Anne, Therese and Visitation (the Johnstown neighbours without homepages); DuckDuckGo searches for the parish, its pastor and its two street addresses (they return only listing sites such as catholicmasstime.org and the directory pages); and the latest bulletins of the neighbouring Johnstown parishes read in this and earlier batches (St. Therese, St. Anne, Visitation, St. Benedict, Resurrection, Our Mother of Sorrows), none of which carries a Gregory and Barnabas schedule. Whether one of the other Johnstown bulletins I did not read (St. Clement, St. Francis of Assisi, the cathedral) carries it is not settled, but nothing links them to this pastor.

## Worship sites

Two: St. Gregory, 120 Boltz Street, and St. Barnabas, 408 Luzon Avenue (Bon Air). Both appear in the directory, GCatholic, the Discover Mass page and third-party Mass-time listings (catholicmasstime.org: "St. Gregory: -Saturday 4:00 PM and Sunday 10:00 AM ... St. Barnabas: -Sunday - 8 AM", weekdays "Monday 5:30 PM & Tuesday 8:00 AM" and "Thursday 5:30 PM & Friday 8:00 AM", agreeing with the directory). Mass times are therefore from the directory only, not from a bulletin.

## Website and bulletin provider

`bulletin_provider: no_bulletin`. The website field holds the parish Facebook page because the field is required and unique; no bulletin was seen there (login wall), so it does not meet the "bulletin actually posted there" rule for a Facebook `website`, and the row stays off the site (Settled policy 4).

""",website=FB,bulletin_provider='no_bulletin',revisit='Look for a weekly bulletin: the parish Facebook page (login wall in the sandbox) or the parish office, 814-536-6818.',revisit_after='2027-01-15')

 dict(url='https://discovermass.com/church/st-gregory-johnstown-pa/',seen=S,quote='Please see the times below for',note='Discover Mass page "Ss. Gregory and Barnabas", 120 Boltz Street, Johnstown, PA 15902, (814) 536-6818: "SS Gregory and Barnabas invites you to celebrate Mass with us; Please see the times below for St. Gregory."'),
 dict(url='https://catholicmasstime.org/church/st-barnabas/6853',seen=S,quote='St. Gregory: -Saturday 4:00 PM and Sunday 10:00 AM',note='Third-party listing; same as the directory. A second aggregator (catholicchurch.directory) gives Monday 6:30 PM where the directory and this one give 5:30 PM.'),
],"""
## Holds Mass

Yes, per the directory (Saturday 4:00 PM; Sunday 10:00 AM; Monday 5:30 PM; Tuesday 8:00 AM; Wednesday private Mass) and the Discover Mass page, which invites visitors to "celebrate Mass with us" at St. Gregory; an advertisement in the 8 March 2026 St. Therese bulletin shows the church hosting a Lenten fish fry. GCatholic "St. Gregory" and the directory "Saint Gregory", 120 Boltz Street, agree, and the Discover Mass page gives 120 Boltz Street, Johnstown, PA 15902 for the parish. ParishesOnline's organization also has 120 Boltz St. `name_verified` and `address_verified` stay false: the parish's own bulletin or site was not available to confirm. Coordinates are the GCatholic Plus Code point.

 dict(url='https://catholicmasstime.org/church/st-barnabas/6853',seen=S,quote='St. Barnabas -Thursday 5:30 PM & Friday 8:00 AM',note='Third-party listing for "Ss.  dict(url='https://sttheresejohnstown.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/STTHERESESBULLETIN-Mar-8-2026-BP.pdf',seen=S,quote='SS Gregory & Barnabas Fish Fry',note='Ad in the 8 March 2026 St. Therese bulletin naming "St Barnabas 408 Luzon Ave" as a Lenten fish-fry site.'),
],"""
## Holds Mass

Yes, per the directory (Sunday 8:00 AM; Thursday 5:30 PM; Friday 8:00 AM) and a third-party listing that agrees; GCatholic lists it; a March 2026 advertisement in the St. Therese bulletin names it as a parish site. No parish bulletin was found, so the times are not confirmed by one (see the parish record, `no_bulletin`).

GCatholic "St. Barnabas" and the directory "Saint Barnabas", 408 Luzon Avenue, Johnstown PA 15902, agree; ParishesOnline has "St. Barnabas Church, 408 Luzon Ave" and the St. Therese ad "408 Luzon Ave". """)

Preview (first 2KB):
# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.

content.content:
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
- A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo
  had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while
  St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish
  one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin
  after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7
  bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row).
- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single
  bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate.

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

**One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories,
chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a
year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building
whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said
St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday
Mass there.

**Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help`
lists them):

| reason | use it for |
|---|---|
| `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) |
| `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down |
| `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels |
| `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church |
| `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) |
| `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what |

An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If
everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`.

**Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather
than reopening them):

1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there.
   A page that merely exists is not enough.
2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church
   moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed`
   column.
3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence
   goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it.
4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its
   churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves
   them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about
   until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as
   accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a
   bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows
   were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own
   goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before.

## Files

```
data/dioceses/<diocese>/
  diocese.md            sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log
  parishes/<slug>.md    one per bulletin publisher      -> a data/parishes.csv row
  churches/<slug>.md    one per worship site            -> a data/churches.csv row
  excluded/<slug>.md    looked at and ruled out, with a reason
  open/<slug>.md        found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it
  rosters/<name>.json   outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools)
```

Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the
files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and
an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese
validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`,
`exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they
would add a validation error.

```markdown
---
name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org
bulletin_provider: parishes_online
provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202
publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091]
group: ''
evidence:
- url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf
  seen: 2026-09-25
  quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm'
  note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone.
---

## Publisher

The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline...
```

`syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight
parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into
shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess.

### Fields

Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with
`revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due.

**parish**
- `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset).
- `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`,
  `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy
  4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by
  `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/<slug>`, the church slug
  from `discovermass.com/church/<slug>/`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive`
  from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for
  `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`,
  `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page,
  or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run
  `pnpm fetch:check --diocese <d> --parish <slug>` (which reads the rows from these
  records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is
  this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README).
- `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never
  share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin
  carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form
  you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:<slug>`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are
  one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:<site id>`, `discovermass:<slug>`, or
  `url:<page>` for a self-hosted bulletin.
- `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`.
- `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and
  `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows.

**church**
- `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills
  them after promotion).
- `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`,
  `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`.
- `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the
  parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are
  others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.**
  Don't pick a favourite without saying so.
- `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `<roster>:<id>`. Written by
  `coverage --link` or by hand.

**excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`,
`decided`, `roster`.

**open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`.

**evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A
`quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck`
fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found.

## The explanation

The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file
and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check
each claim and see where your judgement came in.

**Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1)
names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be.
Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a
homepage will be different next month.

**Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five
buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak:
Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once.
When your evidence is absence, list what you checked.

**When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it,
which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next
door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was
written down.

What batch 14 found:
- **St. Anne and St. Therese** share one website but publish two separate bulletins, so they are two rows. Both downloaded in the check. The weak spot: the fetcher picks a file by its date and place in the list, not its name. Each row therefore relies on its own bulletin being listed first on a different page of the site. If the parish reorders its pages, one row could pick up the other parish's bulletin. I've written this risk into both records and will list a file-name filter as a suggested improvement in the PR.

content.content:
---
name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
  Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City;
  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.
- **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of
  them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory
  (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists
  churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John
  chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary,
  Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin.
- **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral
  plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above.
- **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org
  (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap)
  mention no closures or mergers.

### Bulletin publishers here

Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows
otherwise.

- **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken
  (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`)
  list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is
  `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 =
  not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the
  directory lacks. A joint bulletin may sit under only one of its churches' slugs (Our Lady
  Queen of Angels, Central City carries the issue for Holy Family, Hooversville and All Saints,
  Boswell, whose own pages are empty): a no-homepage parish can be a worship site of a
  neighbour's row, so read the neighbours' mastheads before calling it `no_bulletin`. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St.
  Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a
  chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids.
- **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS,
  stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and
  stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist
  with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St.
  Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several
  church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte
  "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as
  `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church
  page, not a tokenised download link.
- **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www.<domain>/bulletins` usually opens in
  headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged.
- **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins
  (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API
  (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`)
  lists organizations near a point.
- **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly;
  `page-pdfs` on the site reads it.
- **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=<id>`, PDFs at `pdfs/<id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`):
  broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/<id>`):
  a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/
  <code>`): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive.
- **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (container 14/0551). Empty orgs: Roaring
  Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones.
- **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph,
  Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin`
  rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an
  empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages
  (`<name>.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS
  (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo
  snippet via `visit.py` reads them.
- **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton;
  `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one.
- **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip
  and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale).
- **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works;
  curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/<any-slug>` answers 200 with a
  generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing.
- **WebParish is live for several parishes** (St. Thomas, Bedford; St. Anthony and St. Elizabeth
  Ann Seton, Windber, `PDFs MMDDYY.pdf` and `SEAS<YYYY-MM-DD>Bulletin.pdf`). A parish's own
  domain can redirect to its WebParish site (stelizabethannsetonwindber.com). For a parish with
  no directory homepage, a DuckDuckGo search (`uv run python visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..."`)
  finds these. Sister parishes with one pastor can each post a bulletin listing the same
  combined Mass rota (Windber): two rows while both channels are live.
- For St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to
  `webparish.com/aj/<name>/index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists
  `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it.
- **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18
  Oct issue was not up on 21 Oct): `newest-recent` is then expected, not a fault.
- **2MHost** (stjohneverettpa.org) uses `<base href>`; the fetch code honours it since batch 7.
- **`probe pdf` can't take a URL with spaces**: pass `%20`.
- **Nominatim** answers through the sandbox (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?street=..&city=..
  &state=..&format=json`, with a user agent): use it to tell which of two GCatholic points is
  the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors,
  Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968).
- **webparish.com/aj/<name>/** answers 406 (Mod_Security) to curl; headed Chrome needs the
  explicit `/index.php`. It is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi,
  Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing
  to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow
  the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home.
- **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael,
  Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every
  time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works.
- **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859),
  St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare
  403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try,
  and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:<id>` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date
  files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`).
- **Wix image bulletins** (St. Anne, Davidsville): one JPEG per week on the Bulletin page,
  alt text `MMDDYYYY.jpg`; `page-images <page>` reads it (the date parser takes MMDDYYYY since
  batch 9). St. Peter, Somerset: PHP `bulletin.php` linking `site_docs/<n>.pdf`. New Baltimore:
  WordPress, posts about a week late.
- **Partner bulletins:** in Johnstown both no-homepage parishes in batch 12 (St. Patrick; St.
  Michael) are carried in their pastor's other parish's bulletin. Read the partner's cover
  first. A parish domain redirecting to the partner's site (stpatrickjtown.com → the
  cathedral; `probe url` says REDIRECT-OFFSITE) is a fold-in, not a squat.
- **Duda** (the Johnstown cathedral, `irp.cdn-website.com`) resets curl intermittently; retry.
  Its `/welcome#WeeklyBulletin` lists `files/uploaded/YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` (not always zero-padded).
  omostoday.com (WordPress/Elementor) posts scanned issues: render with `pdftoppm`.
- **Two parishes on one site** (St. Therese and St. Anne, sttheresejohnstown.com, one PDF each
  per week): recipes can't filter by file name, so each row points at a different page whose
  list puts its own PDF first (homepage vs `/bulletins/`), with `#fragment` publication ids to
  keep them distinct. Fragile: re-check both picks if the site reorders.
- **WordPress PDF Embedder** (Visitation BVM, Johnstown, found by DuckDuckGo) turns PDF links
  into canvases; `page-pdfs <site>/category/<cat>/feed/` reads the RSS feed instead.
- **Third-party Mass-time aggregators** (catholicmasstime.org, catholicchurch.directory)
  disagree with each other and the directory: never a second source.
- **An eCatholic id on a site doesn't mean the bulletin is there**: standrewjohnstown.org is
  eCatholic (36351) but its bulletin folder is empty and its Bulletins menu goes to Discover Mass.
- **Self-hosted, odd hosts:** SiteGround WordPress (mhtcc.org, Huntingdon; stbenedictchurch.org,
  Johnstown; `tools/browser_get.py <page> <pdf> <out>` downloads a PDF through Chrome) drops `probe pdf`
  and plain-http curl (RemoteDisconnected or an sgcaptcha page); use https with a Chrome user
  agent, or `visit.py --bulletin`. Homestead (scosmu.org, Mount Union) resets https; `http://www.`
  works, PDFs named `<Month>_<D>.pdf` on its About-Us page.
- **findglocal.com/US/<town>/<id>/<page>** mirrors a Facebook page's posts and Mass times
  without a login: useful evidence for `no_bulletin` parishes (Dudley).
- **College campus Masses** (Juniata College, Tussey Hall) appear in the directory's Mass
  times but in no bulletin: `open/` until someone confirms they are public.
- **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans).
  `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a
  quote, and says so.
- **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in
  the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a
  second source before verifying.
- **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/),
  Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date).
- **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona
  cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads.
  Cite that page directly.
- `tools/fill_record.py` fills evidence and body into a new record (see the tools README).
- `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them.

## Rules settled for this diocese

Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them.

## Log

Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

The website field holds the parish Facebook page because the field is required and unique; no bulletin was seen there (login wall), so it does not meet the "bulletin actually posted there" rule for a Facebook `website`, and the row stays off the site (Settled policy 4).

"The Pharisees went off and plotted how they might entrap 
him in speech. They sent their disciples to him, with the 
Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are a truthful 
man and that you teach the way of God in accordance with the 
truth. And you are not concerned with anyone’s opinion, for 
you do not regard a person’s status. Tell us, then, what is your 
opinion: Is it lawful to pay the census tax to Caesar or not?”  
Matthew 22:15–17
The Herodians were a political group who supported the rule 
of Herod Antipas and his dynasty. They favored collaboration 
with the Roman Empire and upheld the Herodian line as the 
legitimate rulers over Judea. For the sake of national stability, 
they promoted political compromise.
The Pharisees, on the other hand, were a religious sect devoted 
to the Law of Moses and the strict observance of Jewish 
customs, though often corrupted by legalism. They viewed 
Gentile rule as a threat to the sanctity of God’s covenant and 
wielded great influence over the people due to their outward 
piety and perceived religious authority.
Given their stark political and theological differences, the 
alliance formed between the Pharisees and the Herodians in 
their plot against Jesus is both startling and revealing. Despite 
their longstanding enmity, they found common ground in their 
mutual hatred of Jesus. The Pharisees sought to undermine His 
credibility among the people, while the Herodians hoped to 
present Him as a threat to Roman authority. Together, they 
constructed a trap, hoping Jesus would either speak against the 
Law or against Caesar—either of which would serve their 
purposes. Hatred, envy, jealousy, pride, and self-righteousness 
can forge what appears to be unity—even among rivals—but 
it is a unity rooted in darkness, a counterfeit communion built 
on shared agendas rather than truth. It is the kind of alliance 
in which satan himself rejoices. Such false unity always 
unravels. Anything built on pride and sin cannot stand. Unity 
can only endure where truth, humility, and love prevail.
As we look around us, we see many such counterfeit alliances 
formed not by shared conviction in what is good and true, but 
by convenience in opposing what threatens personal 
influence or power. Individuals and groups unite to silence 
voices that speak uncomfortable truths. This is frequently 
seen in politics and culture, but is also tragically found even 
within the Church. In every case, truth is twisted, motives are 
disguised, and God’s pure and holy will becomes the object 
of attack. When such unholy alliances take root within the 
Church, they do grave damage to our common mission to 
proclaim the Gospel in truth.
True Christian unity is not grounded in shared ambitions or 
human agendas, but in the Person of Jesus Christ. It is 
expressed through charity, humility, and fidelity to God’s 
will. It is not built on calculation or convenience but on the 
self-emptying love of Christ, who calls us to die to self and 
live for Him. Our only agenda must be that God be glorified 
and His children drawn into His glory and sanctification. As 
members of His Body, the Church, our unity must reflect the 
communion of the Most Holy Trinity, rooted in divine love, 
not in political expediency or pride.

description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of th
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

## Setup, once per sandbox (~1 min)

```bash
.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh
```

This installs Google Chrome and trusts the agent proxy's TLS certificate in Chrome's store.
Before it runs, no browser starts at all:

- The venv's Playwright wants a newer Chromium than the image ships, and
  `playwright install` is blocked.
- The proxy re-terminates TLS, so every page fails with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`.

## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser

```bash
V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py"
uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org   # like probe url
uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic
uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png   # Read the PNG
```

It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered**
HTML of the page and its iframes:

- **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
  NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means
  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,
  and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF.
- **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5)
  until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no
  publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:<the page that lists them>`. That page
  may be an index linking one post per issue, or the home page itself.
- **`--follow TEXT`** clicks through to the first link whose text or href contains TEXT
  (repeatable, one URL only). The page it lands on goes under `followed`; the top-level
  fields still describe the site. Prefer a path (`/bulletins`) to a word: "bulletin" also

## Publisher

St. Therese of the Child Jesus publishes its own weekly bulletin on the shared parish WordPress site sttheresejohnstown.com. The 18 Oct 2026 issue (`STTHERESESBULLETIN-Oct-18-2026-BP.pdf`, read 2026-10-21) is headed "ST. THERESE OF THE CHILD JESUS / THE CHURCH OF THE FRANCISCANS / FR. BERNARD KARMANOCKY, OFM, PASTOR" and lists Mass intentions only for St. Therese (Mon-Fri 7:50AM, Sat 4:00PM, Sun 7:30AM and 10:30AM). No other church's Masses appear in it.

**One bulletin or two?** The pastor and the website are shared with St. Anne (Fr. Karmanocky is pastor of both), which suggested one bulletin. It is two: the site publishes a separate PDF for each church every week (`STTHERESESBULLETIN-<Mon>-<D>-2026-BP.pdf` and `St-Annes-Bulletin-<Mon>-<D>.pdf`, Aug through Oct 2026 on the Bulletins page). The 18 Oct St. Anne issue is headed "ST. ANNE'S CHURCH", with its own intentions (Sat 5:30PM, Sun 9:00AM, weekdays 7:00AM), lectors and notes. The two issues share the Paluch reflection and some announcements, but each is a separate file naming its own church, so by the rules they are separate rows (this one and `saint-anne-johnstown`).

import sys,re
# usage: fill.py record.md evidence.yaml body.md [set key=value ...]
p,ev,body=sys.argv[1:4]
sets=dict(a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[4:])
t=open(p).read()
m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n',t,re.S)
fm=m.group(1)
evt=open(ev).read().rstrip('\n')
if re.search(r'^evidence: \[\]$',fm,re.M):
    fm=re.sub(r'^evidence: \[\]$','evidence:\n'+evt,fm,flags=re.M)
else:
    fm=fm+'\n'+evt
for k,v in sets.items():
    if re.search(rf'^{k}:.*$',fm,re.M): fm=re.sub(rf'^{k}:.*$',f'{k}: {v}',fm,flags=re.M)
    else: fm+=f'\n{k}: {v}'
open(p,'w').write('---\n'+fm+'\n---\n\n'+open(body).read().strip('\n')+'\n')
