## Publisher

Four canonical parishes with one pastor, Rev. Joseph C. Nale (St. John the Baptist, Summerhill; Immaculate Conception, New Germany; Most Holy Trinity, South Fork; St. Bartholomew, Wilmore), publish **one** weekly bulletin, posted on the Summerhill/New Germany site stjic.org (WordPress; PDFs at `www.stjic.org/wp-content/uploads/<YYYY>/<MM>/<Month>-<D>-<YYYY>.pdf`, listed on https://www.stjic.org/bulletins/). The 18 October 2026 issue (2 pages, read 2026-10-21) is headed "Fr. Joseph C. Nale, Pastor", with the contact block for all four churches ("ST. JOHN THE BAPTIST 540 Main St. Summerhill, Pa ... IMMACULATE CONCEPTION 1640 New Germany Rd. New Germany, Pa ... MOST HOLY TRINITY 550 Main St. South Fork, Pa ... ST. BARTHOLOMEW 185 Church Hill, Wilmore, Pa") and one "MASSES FOR THE WEEK" list coded SJ, IC, MHT and SB, plus one liturgical-minister schedule, one offertory table and one Catholic Ministry Drive table covering all four. The 11 October issue has the identical masthead and a rota for all four. So there is one bulletin and one row, not four.

None of the other three has a separate channel: the old homepage of Most Holy Trinity (GCatholic's mostholytrinitychurch.com) now redirects to a domain-sale page, and the Discover Mass pages for Most Holy Trinity (`most-holy-trinity-south-fork-pa`), St. Bartholomew (`st-bartholomew-wilmore-pa`) and St. John the Baptist (`st-john-the-baptist-summerhill-pa`) all say "Shucks! There are no bulletins available" (read 2026-10-21). The diocese's directory gives no homepage for South Fork and Wilmore. Their Facebook pages are named in the bulletin ("Saint Bartholomew Catholic Church", "Most Holy Trinity Catholic Church"); not opened (login wall).

## Worship sites

Four churches, all in the bulletin's Mass list: St. John the Baptist (Summerhill), Immaculate Conception (New Germany, which the diocese's directory files under Summerhill), Most Holy Trinity (South Fork) and St. Bartholomew (Wilmore). Nothing the directory or GCatholic lists for these four parishes is left out. The Byzantine St. Michael the Archangel, South Fork (Discover Mass `st-michael-the-archangel-byzantine-south-fork-pa`) is Eastern Catholic and not part of this row.

## Website and bulletin provider

`website` is https://www.stjic.org, the diocese's homepage for St. John the Baptist and Immaculate Conception. The site is plain WordPress, so the row is `other`, read by the recipe `page-pdfs https://www.stjic.org/bulletins/` (fetch:check 2026-10-21: picked October-18-2026.pdf, url_date 2026-10-18, 469,636 bytes, current). Publication id is `url:https://www.stjic.org/bulletins/`.

## Not yet confirmed

The site is a St. John / Immaculate Conception site and carries no South Fork or Wilmore pages; the cover of the bulletin is the only place all four are tied together. If South Fork and Wilmore ever start a bulletin of their own (the Discover Mass pages exist but are empty), split them out.

## Holds Mass

Yes. The 18 October 2026 bulletin of the shared row lists SJ Masses Monday 7:45 AM, Wednesday 7:45 AM (that day "NO MASS"), Saturday 5:30 PM and Sunday 8:30 AM, and the stjic.org home page lists "SJ - Mass Schedule Mon, Wed, Sat & Sun" (read 2026-10-21). The diocese's directory has Saturday 5:30 PM, Sunday 8:30 AM and Monday 7:45 AM, which matches.

## Name and address

Name: GCatholic, the directory, the bulletin and OSM all say St. John the Baptist. Address: sources split on the street number of one building. GCatholic 23888 and the directory say 538 Main Street; the bulletin masthead, the site's header and OSM (way 1414142315) say 540 Main Street; stjic.org's footer says 538. Same town and ZIP (15958). Followed 538, the directory/GCatholic number, and left `address_verified` false because the numbers disagree; the rectory/PO Box is Box 248. content.content:
## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser

```bash
V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py"
uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org   # like probe url
uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic
uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png   # Read the PNG
```

It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered**
HTML of the page and its iframes:

- **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
  NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means
  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,
  and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF.
- **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5)
  until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no
  publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:<the page that lists them>`. That page
  may be an index linking one post per issue, or the home page itself.
- **`--follow TEXT`** clicks through to the first link whose text or href contains TEXT
  (repeatable, one URL only). The page it lands on goes under `followed`; the top-level
  fields still describe the site. Prefer a path (`/bulletins`) to a word: "bulletin" also
  matches "Publish in our Bulletin".
- **`--text` (`--chars N`), `--links` (`--match REGEX`), `--html PATH` and
  `--screenshot PATH`** read the final page. With several URLs, the file names get `-0`,
  `-1` and so on.

What it found on the 21 Syracuse sites `probe url` couldn't read (2026-09-25):

- **Behind Cloudflare:** eCatholic ids for two (`ecatholic:35905`, `ecatholic:33641`).
- **In "Bulletins" pages or widgets:** ParishesOnline ids for three (`po-org:…`, `lpi:…`,
  `po-container:…`).
- **Self-hosted:** three bulletins.
- **Dead or hijacked domains:** a parked domain, a for-sale page, and a site taken over by a
  Chinese movie-streaming page. None of these contain parish words, so they get a non-`ok`
  verdict.
- **Never loaded:** two sites stayed BLOCKED through every run (see the next section).

import sys,re
# usage: fill.py record.md evidence.yaml body.md [set key=value ...]
p,ev,body=sys.argv[1:4]
sets=dict(a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[4:])
t=open(p).read()
m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n',t,re.S)
fm=m.group(1)

- `discovermass-church-urls.txt`: all 20,279 Discover Mass church page URLs (from `wp-sitemap-posts-item-1..11.xml` on discovermass.com, 2026-10-21); `grep -i <town>` finds a church's slug when `?s=` search is broken. A page's "Visit Website" link gives the parish's homepage.

Run with `python3 -I`. Quote any `quote:` value containing ": " yourself.
- `browser_get.py <referer-page> <file-url> <out>`: downloads a PDF with the fetch pipeline's own HTTP client (SiteGround sgcaptchas curl and `probe pdf` on stbenedictchurch.org PDFs, but not this); run with `uv run python`, then `pdftotext`.

Preview (first 2KB):
# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.

content.content:
| `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `:` to the record's `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones. 8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed. 9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate `, `pnpm diocese todo `, a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit. **Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote ` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set: the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes"). Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`). Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and `verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned. `pnpm diocese recheck ` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago. ## Traps Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once. - **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the masthead. - **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin. `validate` rejects the truncated form. - **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare mastheads. - **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live. - **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise the publisher just changed. - **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short. - **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it. - **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works. `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS. - **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check the URL before you store it. - **Directory street numbers are sometimes PO boxes** ("1154 Lower College Dr" was "PO Box 1154"), and one building can have an address on two streets. - **A summarizing fetch tool is not a source.** For a quote, read the page itself (`probe pdf`, `curl`, the recheck tool). One summary moved a 2020 merger to 2026. The article's weekdays gave the real year. - **A hand-written `quote:` or `note:` containing ": " breaks the YAML.** Quote the value (`note: 'Page 1: the masthead'`). `validate` catches it, but only after the whole file is unreadable, which in Albany briefly left three churches pointing at a "missing" parish. - **Coverage measures the roster.** A place the roster doesn't list moves no number, and an oratory with no weekend Mass can be missing from every list and still be open. `coverage` lists your churches that are in no roster; each needs an explanation, not deletion. ## Commands `pnpm diocese --help` gives every flag. Output is JSON (`pnpm --silent` drops pnpm's banner for `jq`). Without pnpm: `uv run python -m pdf_extract diocese ...`. ```bash pnpm diocese list | show | todo | validate [] pnpm diocese init --name "..." --state NY [--website URL] [--gcatholic key] pnpm diocese search [--diocese d|live] [--kind parish|church|excluded|open] pnpm diocese new parish --name ... --website ... [--bulletin-provider p --provider-id id --publication x:y --group g] pnpm diocese new church --parish

[--from roster:id ...] [--name ... --line1 ... --city ... ...] pnpm diocese new excluded --reason [--from roster:id] [--name ... --city ... --last-mass date] pnpm diocese new open --name ... --revisit "next step" [--revisit-after date] [--from roster:id] pnpm diocese merge ... --into [--note "why"] pnpm diocese rename pnpm diocese exclude --reason [--last-mass date] pnpm diocese question --revisit "next step" [--revisit-after date]

name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
  Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City;
  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.
- **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of
  them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory
  (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists
  churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John
  chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary,
  Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin.
- **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral
  plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above.
- **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org
  (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap)
  mention no closures or mergers.

### Bulletin publishers here

Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows
otherwise.

- **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken
  (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`)
  list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is
  `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 =
  not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the
  directory lacks. A joint bulletin may sit under only one of its churches' slugs (Our Lady
  Queen of Angels, Central City carries the issue for Holy Family, Hooversville and All Saints,
  Boswell, whose own pages are empty): a no-homepage parish can be a worship site of a
  neighbour's row, so read the neighbours' mastheads before calling it `no_bulletin`. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St.
  Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a
  chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids.
- **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS,
  stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and
  stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist
  with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St.
  Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several
  church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte
  "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as
  `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church
  page, not a tokenised download link.
- **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www.<domain>/bulletins` usually opens in
  headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged.
- **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins
  (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API
  (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`)
  lists organizations near a point.
- **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly;
  `page-pdfs` on the site reads it.
- **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=<id>`, PDFs at `pdfs/<id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`):
  broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/<id>`):
  a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/
  <code>`): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive.
- **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (14/0551), St. Clement, Johnstown (14/1971, image
  pages) and St. John Vianney/Transfiguration (14/1788). tesseract is not installed: render pages
  with `pdftoppm` and read them.
- **`dated-post <bulletin page>`** reads a site with one child page per issue (St. Francis of
  Assisi, Johnstown, /bulletin-3/; unpinned `page-pdfs` picked a 2021 PDF). Empty orgs: Roaring
  Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones.
- **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph,
  Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin`
  rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an
  empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages
  (`<name>.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS
  (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo
  snippet via `visit.py` reads them.
- **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton;
  `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one.
- **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip
  and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale).
- **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works;
  curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/<any-slug>` answers 200 with a
  generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing.
- **WebParish is live for several parishes** (St. Thomas, Bedford; St. Anthony and St. Elizabeth
  Ann Seton, Windber, `PDFs MMDDYY.pdf` and `SEAS<YYYY-MM-DD>Bulletin.pdf`). A parish's own
  domain can redirect to its WebParish site (stelizabethannsetonwindber.com). For a parish with
  no directory homepage, a DuckDuckGo search (`uv run python visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..."`)
  finds these. Sister parishes with one pastor can each post a bulletin listing the same
  combined Mass rota (Windber): two rows while both channels are live.
- For St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to
  `webparish.com/aj/<name>/index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists
  `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it.
- **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18
  Oct issue was not up on 21 Oct): `newest-recent` is then expected, not a fault.
- **2MHost** (stjohneverettpa.org) uses `<base href>`; the fetch code honours it since batch 7.
- **`probe pdf` can't take a URL with spaces**: pass `%20`.
- **Two homepages, one bulletin:** the two Cresson parishes' separate Weebly sites both point at
  one ParishesOnline org (14/1078). Follow each site's "Weekly Bulletin" link before making two rows.
- **Campus and shrine Masses** (Mount Aloysius College; Saint Francis University's chapel; the
  Loretto shrine's summer Sunday Mass) go to `open/` until a source says they are public.
- **One pastor, one bulletin is common in Cambria**: Fr. Nale's stjic.org bulletin carries all
  four of his parishes (Summerhill, New Germany, South Fork, Wilmore), whose own Discover Mass
  pages are empty. Directory Mass times lag the bulletin there by up to two hours.
- **Nominatim** `q=<church name>+<town>` finds church nodes where `street=` fails.
- **Nominatim** answers through the sandbox (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?street=..&city=..
  &state=..&format=json`, with a user agent): use it to tell which of two GCatholic points is
  the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors,
  Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968).
- **webparish.com/aj/<name>/** answers 406 (Mod_Security) to curl; headed Chrome needs the
  explicit `/index.php`. It is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi,
  Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing
  to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow
  the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home.
- **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael,
  Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every
  time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works.
- **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859),
  St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare
  403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try,
  and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:<id>` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date
  files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`).
- **Wix image bulletins** (St. Anne, Davidsville): one JPEG per week on the Bulletin page,
  alt text `MMDDYYYY.jpg`; `page-images <page>` reads it (the date parser takes MMDDYYYY since
  batch 9). St. Peter, Somerset: PHP `bulletin.php` linking `site_docs/<n>.pdf`. New Baltimore:
  WordPress, posts about a week late.
- **Partner bulletins:** in Johnstown both no-homepage parishes in batch 12 (St. Patrick; St.
  Michael) are carried in their pastor's other parish's bulletin. Read the partner's cover
  first. A parish domain redirecting to the partner's site (stpatrickjtown.com → the
  cathedral; `probe url` says REDIRECT-OFFSITE) is a fold-in, not a squat.
- **Duda** (the Johnstown cathedral, `irp.cdn-website.com`) resets curl intermittently; retry.
  Its `/welcome#WeeklyBulletin` lists `files/uploaded/YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` (not always zero-padded).
  omostoday.com (WordPress/Elementor) posts scanned issues: render with `pdftoppm`.
- **Two parishes on one site** (St. Therese and St. Anne, sttheresejohnstown.com, one PDF each
  per week): recipes can't filter by file name, so each row points at a different page whose
  list puts its own PDF first (homepage vs `/bulletins/`), with `#fragment` publication ids to
  keep them distinct. Fragile: re-check both picks if the site reorders.
- **WordPress PDF Embedder** (Visitation BVM, Johnstown, found by DuckDuckGo) turns PDF links
  into canvases; `page-pdfs <site>/category/<cat>/feed/` reads the RSS feed instead.
- **Third-party Mass-time aggregators** (catholicmasstime.org, catholicchurch.directory)
  disagree with each other and the directory: never a second source.
- **An eCatholic id on a site doesn't mean the bulletin is there**: standrewjohnstown.org is
  eCatholic (36351) but its bulletin folder is empty and its Bulletins menu goes to Discover Mass.
- **Self-hosted, odd hosts:** SiteGround WordPress (mhtcc.org, Huntingdon; stbenedictchurch.org,
  Johnstown; `tools/browser_get.py <page> <pdf> <out>` downloads a PDF through Chrome) drops `probe pdf`
  and plain-http curl (RemoteDisconnected or an sgcaptcha page); use https with a Chrome user
  agent, or `visit.py --bulletin`. Homestead (scosmu.org, Mount Union) resets https; `http://www.`
  works, PDFs named `<Month>_<D>.pdf` on its About-Us page.
- **findglocal.com/US/<town>/<id>/<page>** mirrors a Facebook page's posts and Mass times
  without a login: useful evidence for `no_bulletin` parishes (Dudley).
- **College campus Masses** (Juniata College, Tussey Hall) appear in the directory's Mass
  times but in no bulletin: `open/` until someone confirms they are public.
- **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans).
  `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a
  quote, and says so.
- **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in
  the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a
  second source before verifying.
- **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/),
  Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date).
- **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona
  cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads.
  Cite that page directly.
- `tools/fill_record.py` fills evidence and body into a new record (see the tools README).
- `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them.

## Rules settled for this diocese

Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them.

## Log

Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

content.content:
Holy Family Parish, once known as Saint Joseph Parish, is the current site of all the Roman Catholic Parishes that were originally in Portage.  Those parishes were, Sacred Heart, Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Saint John the Baptist, and of course, Saint Joseph.  On September 9, 1999, Sacred Heart, Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary and Saint John the Baptist Parishes merged to become Our Lady of the Sacred Heart.  In 2004, Saint John the Baptist was relegated to profane but not sordid use.  On August 17, 2015, Saint Joseph Parish and Our Lady of the Sacred Heart officially merged.  With the completion of renovations and remodeling, Saint Joseph Church was renamed Holy Family Church.  The Rededication of the Church and Consecration of the Altar was celebrated on June 19, 2016.

== https://apnews.com/general-news-274ce1c595d04e77987fcba3cbac848c

== https://cs.observer-reporter.com/news/2017/mar/12/borough-urges-reuse-of-churches
200
Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Church of Our Lady of Sacred Heart Parish, 806 Hammer St., Portage is shown Thursday.
The sun rises behind the former Sacred Heart of Jesus Church on Mountain Avenue, Portage, Thursday. The former church was part of Our Lady of Sacred Heart Parish.
Council voted last week to explore revoking tax-exempt status for the former Our Lady of the Sacred Heart Parish church and a former church school.
Our Lady of the Sacred Heart was merged with the former St. Joseph Church in 2015, combining three former active congregations into one, renamed the Holy Family Parish.
Mass is now held in the former St. Joseph building on Caldwell Avenue.
Both Sacred Heart parish church buildings remain vacant and are listed for sale, along with the former school.
They include the former Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Church on Hammers Street and the former Sacred Heart of Jesus Church on Mountain Avenue at Orchard Street. The two were merged in 1999 to create the Our Lady of the Sacred Heart Parish.
The original Sacred Heart church properties on Mountain Avenue include an attached rectory, a former school and two-car garage.
Deeds show the property is owned by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown, in trust for the local congregations. Holy Family continues to pay for utilities and maintenance on the vacant buildings, McCarthy said.
If the sale goes through, Sacred Heart will become the new home for Johnstown’s Holy Cross Parish of the Polish National Catholic Church, 534 Woodland Ave., the Rev. Paul Zomerfeld said.
Zomerfeld said the church put a deposit on the Sacred Heart Property and the sale was accepted by Holy Family. He has contacted the diocese numerous times about the delay, but received no answers.
Although he said he does not know why the sale has not been finalized, he said the relationship with Altoona has a history of tension. When Johnstown Catholic churches were being closed, Zomerfeld said parishioners were discouraged from moving to the Polish National Catholic Church.
“Both the Diocesan College of Consulters and Finance Council must approve potential sales, and those steps are currently being undertaken with regard to the Holy Family properties.”
== https://www.yahoo.com/news/portages-sacred-heart-jesus-church-223300409.html

Portage's Sacred Heart of Jesus church building razed
Portage's Sacred Heart of Jesus church building razed
Demolition crews have begun working at the former Sacred Heart of Jesus Church in Portage, two years after attempts to find a new owner were halted by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown.
The former Sacred Heart of Jesus Church and the former Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Church were merged in 1999 to create Our Lady of the Sacred Heart Parish, which was later merged with St. Joseph Church in 2015 to create Holy Family Parish.
Demolition crews from G&R Excavating Demolition, of Tyrone, began working this week at the former Sacred Heart of Jesus Church on Mountain Avenue in Portage.
The former Sacred Heart of Jesus Church and the former Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Church on Hammer Street were merged in 1999 to create Our Lady of the Sacred Heart Parish.
That parish was then merged with St. Joseph Church in 2015 to create Holy Family Parish. All functions were consolidated at the former St. Joseph's Caldwell Avenue complex.
At the time, Scott Morris, of Century 21, and the Rev. Paul Zomerfeld, of Holy Cross Polish National Catholic Church in Johnstown's Moxham section, told The Tribune-Democrat that the Johns-town church had made an offer on the Mountain Avenue property and that the offer was accepted by Holy Family Parish.

## Publisher

Saint Francis of Assisi (pastor Fr. Anthony Francis Spilka, OFMConv.) publishes its own weekly bulletin as a PDF on its WordPress site, `stfrancisofassisijohnstown.com`, one page per issue under `/bulletin-3/`. The 18 Oct 2026 issue (read 2026-10-21) is headed "THE FAITH COMMUNITY OF ST. FRANCIS OF ASSISI" and carries only this parish's Masses. It is a self-hosted bulletin (`other`, `page-pdfs` recipe on the Bulletin page).

**Shared-bulletin check (batch 15 lead):** the 18 Oct issue contains no mention of Sts. Gregory, Barnabas, Fr. Elue or St. Clement (text-layer grep, 2026-10-21), so it does not carry the no-bulletin Sts. Gregory and Barnabas row.

**Site quirk:** the server returns HTTP 500 (and 406 to plain curl) while still delivering the page body; `probe url` reports HTTP5XX, headed Chrome reads it.

## Worship sites

One: St. Francis of Assisi, 120 Barron Avenue (see `churches/saint-francis-of-assisi-johnstown.md`). The Activity Center at 134 Barron Avenue is a hall, not a Mass site.

## Website and bulletin provider

`other`, recipe `dated-post https://www.stfrancisofassisijohnstown.com/bulletin-3/`: `fetch:check` on 2026-10-21 picked Bulletin-October-18-2026.pdf ("dated-post ...: current"). The unpinned guess (`page-pdfs`) picked a 2021 testimonial PDF listed first, so the recipe is needed. `website` is the Bulletin page; `publication` is that page's URL.

Preview (first 2KB):
# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.

content.content:
---
name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
  Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City;
  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.
- **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of
  them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory
  (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists
  churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John
  chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary,
  Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin.
- **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral
  plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above.
- **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org
  (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap)
  mention no closures or mergers.

### Bulletin publishers here

Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows
otherwise.

- **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken
  (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`)
  list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is
  `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 =
  not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the
  directory lacks. A joint bulletin may sit under only one of its churches' slugs (Our Lady
  Queen of Angels, Central City carries the issue for Holy Family, Hooversville and All Saints,
  Boswell, whose own pages are empty): a no-homepage parish can be a worship site of a
  neighbour's row, so read the neighbours' mastheads before calling it `no_bulletin`. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St.
  Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a
  chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids.
- **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS,
  stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and
  stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist
  with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St.
  Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several
  church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte
  "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as
  `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church
  page, not a tokenised download link.
- **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www.<domain>/bulletins` usually opens in
  headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged.
- **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins
  (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API
  (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`)
  lists organizations near a point.
- **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly;
  `page-pdfs` on the site reads it.
- **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=<id>`, PDFs at `pdfs/<id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`):
  broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/<id>`):
  a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/
  <code>`): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive.
- **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (14/0551), St. Clement, Johnstown (14/1971, image
  pages) and St. John Vianney/Transfiguration (14/1788). tesseract is not installed: render pages
  with `pdftoppm` and read them.
- **`dated-post <bulletin page>`** reads a site with one child page per issue (St. Francis of
  Assisi, Johnstown, /bulletin-3/; unpinned `page-pdfs` picked a 2021 PDF). Empty orgs: Roaring
  Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones.
- **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph,
  Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin`
  rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an
  empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages
  (`<name>.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS
  (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo
  snippet via `visit.py` reads them.
- **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton;
  `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one.
- **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip
  and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale).
- **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works;
  curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/<any-slug>` answers 200 with a
  generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing.
