## Rules settled for this diocese

Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them.

## Log

Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `:` to the record's `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Expect most unmatched entries to be naming noise (hamlet vs town, parish name vs building name, "St. Jude" vs "St. Jude Chapel"). Add hamlet spellings to `city_aliases` in `diocese.md`. Once linked, an entry stays resolved, so the next run only shows new ones. 8. **Audit structure.** `pnpm diocese audit [--fetch]` lists groups whose churches span several parish rows, and which ones have no `publication` ids to tell them apart. **Run it every session.** It is the only check for Buffalo's most persistent mistake. "Every family has been read" was declared twice while four families that each publish one bulletin sat in the data as fourteen rows. Collapsing them changed no church row and no coverage number, which is why nothing else noticed. 9. **Close the session.** `pnpm diocese validate `, `pnpm diocese todo `, a dated line in `diocese.md`'s *Log* with the coverage numbers, and a commit. **Promotion:** when `todo` shows no errors or incomplete records, run `pnpm diocese promote --dry-run`, read it, then `pnpm diocese promote ` and `pnpm test`. The next pipeline command seeds the new rows into the database. New parish rows go in with `fetch_only` set: the weekly run fetches their bulletins but doesn't process them or show their churches until the flag is cleared (README, "Fetch-only parishes"). Promotion appends new rows, updates promoted ones, and deletes live rows the diocese has retired (merged, renamed, excluded, moved to open/, or `no_bulletin`). Retiring a church deletes its events, and retiring a parish deletes its bulletins and the events read from them, even for churches moved to another parish. The dry run lists the churches that would lose events (`removed_rows_with_events`). Removals don't go live on merge: deploys keep serving the published data, and the next weekly run is held for review. Publishing that run is what applies them. It also keeps coordinates and flags that `geocode` and `verify` filled in. Keep editing the records after promotion and promote again. Don't delete a promoted record: exclude it or merge it, or its live row will be orphaned. `pnpm diocese recheck ` re-fetches every quoted source. Run it when auditing, or before promoting a diocese that was researched a while ago. ## Traps Each of these produced a confident wrong answer in Buffalo at least once. - **A publisher's account name is not a membership list of the present.** LPi footers and ParishesOnline org names build up over time: one container's footer still named two parishes it served under a previous owner and left out one it serves now. Read the masthead. - **LPi ids are 18 characters** (`0018000000Qbyz4AAB`). Matched as digits, every id in a diocese truncates to `00180000` and unrelated parishes look like one bulletin. `validate` rejects the truncated form. - **Comparing files doesn't answer "same bulletin?"**. A parish that hosts its family's bulletin itself serves a file with a different size, hash and even page count. Compare mastheads. - **A missing ParishesOnline issue answers 403, not 404.** "403 every week" means the container is dead only if the same probe finds issues in a container you know is live. - **A silent container means a fold-in only if a live one exists to fold into.** Otherwise the publisher just changed. - **The masthead is often not on page 1.** LPi puts a generic cover reflection first. A container that looks anonymous is usually just a page short. - **Lapsed parish domains get squatted.** Two Buffalo domains were taken by one online-slots network; one redirect was first read as a merger into a family site. `probe url` checks for the vocabulary; read any redirect target before acting on it. - **A DNS failure can be transient**, and a bare domain can fail where `www.` works. `probe url` retries both before reporting DEAD-DNS. - **The diocese's own homepage for a parish can be dead**, and so can the directory's. Check the URL before you store it.

A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of the time, renders JavaScript sites and iframe widget --- # Seeing parish sites the probes can't This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only 7. It couldn't read these: - **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is behind it), or a bot-block. - **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells. - **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget, or on a "Bulletins" page one click away. WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the `scheme:value` form that `publication` takes. ## Setup, once per sandbox (~1 min) ```bash .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh ``` This installs Google Chrome and trusts the agent proxy's TLS certificate in Chrome's store. Before it runs, no browser starts at all: - The venv's Playwright wants a newer Chromium than the image ships, and `playwright install` is blocked. - The proxy re-terminates TLS, so every page fails with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`. ## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser ```bash V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py" uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org # like probe url uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png # Read the PNG ``` It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered** HTML of the page and its iframes: - **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX, NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all: for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis. - **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s. - **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15, and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF. - **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5) until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:`. That page may be an index linking one post per issue, or the home page itself. - **`--follow TEXT`** clicks through to the first link whose text or href contains TEXT (repeatable, one URL only). The page it lands on goes under `followed`; the top-level fields still describe the site. Prefer a path (`/bulletins`) to a word: "bulletin" also

content.content:
`src/pdf_extract/parish_sites/` reads a parish's own site in three stages:

1. **Locate** the bulletin page by following the homepage's "bulletin" links
   (`locate.py`).
2. **Collect** the PDFs it offers (`collectors.py`). Each collector handles one
   way a site offers them: `drive-folder`, `redirected-pdf` (the bulletin link
   is the PDF), `page-pdfs` (links, or addresses in the page's markup),
   `linked-issue-page` (an embedded flipbook or a publisher's listing) and
   `dated-post` (a weekly post that wraps the PDF). They run in that order
   until one finds a convincing set. `page-pdfs` also reads PDF addresses a
   viewer plugin keeps in base64 JSON (PDF Embedder's `pdfemb-data`, 3D
   FlipBook's `FB3D_CLIENT_DATA`), and takes Google Drive files, Google Docs
   (exported as PDF), Concrete CMS and DotNetNuke (`LinkClick.aspx`) downloads
   as PDFs. One more collector runs only when a recipe names it:
   `page-images`, for a parish that posts each issue as an image (a JPEG per
   weekend); `fetch` stores the image as a one-page PDF.
3. **Choose** this week's issue among them (`choose.py`), and say why:
   `current` (dated this week), or a fallback (`newest-recent`, `titled`,
   `first-listed`). `newest-recent` is the newest issue dated in the last 45
   days, taken when the first listed is plainly old, or when it is neither
   dated nor labelled "bulletin" and the page lists a dated series.

Each fetch result records how its bulletin was found ("page-pdfs on
https://…/bulletins: current"), and the run report lists any new bulletin the
site dated, but not this week.

A parish can pin the first two stages with a **recipe** in its `provider_id`:
a collector, a bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`;
a collector alone reads `website` as the bulletin page). A pinned parish skips
the homepage and runs only its collector, so it fails loudly when its site
changes rather than guessing, and no change made for another site can change
what it picks. `fetch:check` prints the recipe that reproduces each pick it
guessed; pin it once the pick is right.

When a site needs something new, add a collector rather than a branch inside
an existing one, and record the site (below).

#### Recorded sites

To keep a resolver change from fixing one site and breaking another, the pages
each resolver read on every parish's real site are recorded in
`tests/fixtures/fetch/<slug>.json.gz`, and `tests/test_fetch_replay.py` replays
them offline against the bulletin in `expected.json`, using each parish's
recipe in `data/parishes.csv` as it is now. After changing `fetch.py` or
`parish_sites/`, or pinning a recipe:

1. Run `pnpm test`. A changed pick on any recorded site fails the replay test.
   A site that now opens a page the old resolver never did fails with "re-record
   this parish".
2. Re-record the sites whose result should change, then check them by hand:

## Publisher

import sys,re
# usage: fill.py record.md evidence.yaml body.md [set key=value ...]
p,ev,body=sys.argv[1:4]
sets=dict(a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[4:])
t=open(p).read()
m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n',t,re.S)
fm=m.group(1)
evt=open(ev).read().rstrip('\n')
if re.search(r'^evidence: \[\]$',fm,re.M):
    fm=re.sub(r'^evidence: \[\]$','evidence:\n'+evt,fm,flags=re.M)
else:
    fm=fm+'\n'+evt
for k,v in sets.items():
    if re.search(rf'^{k}:.*$',fm,re.M): fm=re.sub(rf'^{k}:.*$',f'{k}: {v}',fm,flags=re.M)
    else: fm+=f'\n{k}: {v}'
open(p,'w').write('---\n'+fm+'\n---\n\n'+open(body).read().strip('\n')+'\n')

# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.

content.content:
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs - [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each - [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first - [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo - [Commands](#commands) ## The model **One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is not yet a church, an exclusion or an open question. `--link` saves the automatic matches on their records. For each one left, link it by hand (add `:` to the record's `roster`), or create the church, exclusion or open question. Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

content.content:
---
name: parish-site-access
description: See parish websites and bulletins that `pnpm diocese probe url` can't, while exploring a new diocese from a Claude Code cloud sandbox. A real Chrome (the pipeline's stealth browser, headed under xvfb) that gets past Cloudflare most of th
---

# Seeing parish sites the probes can't

This skill works alongside `explore-diocese`, whose `probe url` fetches pages without a
browser. On Syracuse's 75 parish websites, `probe url` found the bulletin publisher for only
7. It couldn't read these:

- **HTTP4XX (6):** Cloudflare's "Just a moment..." page (every eCatholic-hosted site is
  behind it), or a bot-block.
- **NO-PARISH-WORDS (6):** pages built in JavaScript, or "Redirecting..." shells.
- **`ok` with no publications (most of the rest):** the bulletin sits in an iframe widget,
  or on a "Bulletins" page one click away.

WebFetch hits the same walls. These tools fill the gaps, and they report ids in the
`scheme:value` form that `publication` takes.

## Setup, once per sandbox (~1 min)

```bash
.claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/setup_browser.sh
```

This installs Google Chrome and trusts the agent proxy's TLS certificate in Chrome's store.
Before it runs, no browser starts at all:

- The venv's Playwright wants a newer Chromium than the image ships, and
  `playwright install` is blocked.
- The proxy re-terminates TLS, so every page fails with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`.

## `visit.py`: probe url in a real browser

```bash
V=".claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py"
uv run python $V --bulletin https://www.stmarys-clinton.com http://saintlouisgonzaga.org   # like probe url
uv run python $V https://stleohilton.org --follow /bulletins --links --match files.ecatholic
uv run python $V https://example-parish.org --text --chars 3000 --screenshot /tmp/p.png   # Read the PNG
```

It prints JSON with `probe url`'s fields for the site's own page, judged on the **rendered**
HTML of the page and its iframes:

- **`verdict`:** `probe url`'s checks (SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
  NO-PARISH-WORDS, ok) applied to the rendered HTML, plus two of its own. `BLOCKED` means
  Cloudflare challenged every load. `ERROR` means the browser couldn't load the page at all:
  for example, one Syracuse site answers HTTP 445, which Chrome refuses. A domain that
  doesn't resolve is also `ERROR`; run `probe url` for the DEAD-DNS diagnosis.
- **`publications`:** from the CLI's own `find_publications`, so the ids match `probe url`'s.
- **`bulletin_links`**, and **`pdf_links`** listed separately: `bulletin_links` stops at 15,
  and WordPress pages use those up on feeds before reaching the PDF.
- **`--bulletin`:** when the page embeds no id, it opens the site's bulletin pages (up to 5)
  until one does. The result goes in `bulletin_search.found`. Bulletin PDFs with no
  publisher are reported as self-hosted, with `url:<the page that lists them>`. That page
  may be an index linking one post per issue, or the home page itself.
- **`--follow TEXT`** clicks through to the first link whose text or href contains TEXT
  (repeatable, one URL only). The page it lands on goes under `followed`; the top-level
  fields still describe the site. Prefer a path (`/bulletins`) to a word: "bulletin" also

<a href='https://www.facebook.com/SaintMonicaCatholicChurch/' target='_blank'>Visit Website

SKILL.md

import sys,re
# usage: fill.py record.md evidence.yaml body.md [set key=value ...]
p,ev,body=sys.argv[1:4]
sets=dict(a.split('=',1) for a in sys.argv[4:])
t=open(p).read()
m=re.match(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---\n',t,re.S)
fm=m.group(1)
evt=open(ev).read().rstrip('\n')
if re.search(r'^evidence: \[\]$',fm,re.M):
    fm=re.sub(r'^evidence: \[\]$','evidence:\n'+evt,fm,flags=re.M)
else:
    fm=fm+'\n'+evt
for k,v in sets.items():
    if re.search(rf'^{k}:.*$',fm,re.M): fm=re.sub(rf'^{k}:.*$',f'{k}: {v}',fm,flags=re.M)
    else: fm+=f'\n{k}: {v}'
open(p,'w').write('---\n'+fm+'\n---\n\n'+open(body).read().strip('\n')+'\n')

Preview (first 2KB):
# Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
