content.content:
# Exploring a diocese `data/dioceses//` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`. The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it in a few minutes. This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151 churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both. - [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are - [Files](#files): layout and fields - [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs - [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each - [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first - [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo - [Commands](#commands) ## The model **One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not decide this: - A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one bulletin is **one** row with several churches. - A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows. - A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7 bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row). - A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate. Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin. **One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories, chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday Mass there. **Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help` lists them): | reason | use it for | |---|---| | `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) | | `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down | | `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels | | `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church | | `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) | | `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what | An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`. **Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather than reopening them): 1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there. A page that merely exists is not enough. 2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed` column. 3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it. 4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before. ## Files ``` data/dioceses// diocese.md sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log parishes/.md one per bulletin publisher -> a data/parishes.csv row churches/.md one per worship site -> a data/churches.csv row excluded/.md looked at and ruled out, with a reason open/.md found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it rosters/.json outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools) ``` Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`, `exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they would add a validation error. ```markdown --- name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org bulletin_provider: parishes_online provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202 publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091] group: '' evidence: - url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf seen: 2026-09-25 quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm' note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone. --- ## Publisher The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline... ``` `syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess. ### Fields Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with `revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due. **parish** - `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset). - `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`, `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy 4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/`, the church slug from `discovermass.com/church//`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive` from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`, `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page, or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run `pnpm fetch:check --diocese --parish ` (which reads the rows from these records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README). - `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never share one**, and `validate` enforces that across every diocese: it catches "one bulletin carried as several rows", a mistake that shows up in no other check. Record every form you find: `po-container:14/0434`, `po-org:`, `lpi:<18-character id>` (all three are one ParishesOnline bulletin), `ecatholic:`, `discovermass:`, or `url:` for a self-hosted bulletin. - `group`: the diocese's grouping, e.g. `Family #31`. - `replaces`: slugs of rows merged or renamed into this one. Maintained by `merge` and `rename`; `promote` deletes those live rows. **church** - `parish`, the address fields, `latitude`/`longitude` (or `null`, and `pnpm geocode` fills them after promotion). - `coordinates_from`: `gcatholic-plus-code` (building-precise), `osm-node`, `diocese-directory`, `parishes-online-org`, `nominatim`, `geocode-stage` or `manual`. - `name_verified` / `address_verified`: true only when two independent sources agree (the parish's bulletin and its own site are one source; OSM, GCatholic and the diocese are others). **When sources disagree, leave the flag false and write down the disagreement.** Don't pick a favourite without saying so. - `roster`: the roster entries this place is, as `:`. Written by `coverage --link` or by hand. **excluded**: `reason`, address fields, `parish` (related parish, if any), `last_mass`, `decided`, `roster`. **open**: address fields, `parish`, `roster`, and a required `revisit`. **evidence** items: `url`, `seen` (the date you read it), and `quote` and/or `note`. A `quote` is copied **verbatim** from the page (`…` marks a gap). `pnpm diocese recheck` fetches each URL and checks the quote is still there, so write quotes that can be found. ## The explanation The body of the file is for the person who has to check the row later. They have the file and a browser, and the diocese has moved on since you wrote it. Write so they can re-check each claim and see where your judgement came in. **Every claim has a source, a date and the words.** "The 20 September 2026 masthead (page 1) names the cathedral alone" can be checked. "Single-church parish per the diocese" can't be. Bulletin PDFs at dated URLs never change, which makes them the best evidence there is; a homepage will be different next month. **Say what you read, not what you concluded from.** "The family's Mass schedule lists five buildings and not this one" is evidence. "Not listed" is only absence, and absence is weak: Buffalo's diocesan pages, its masterlist and GCatholic all omitted an open oratory at once. When your evidence is absence, list what you checked. **When sources disagree, write down all of them.** Give each version, which source says it, which one you followed and why, and what would settle it (for example, "the office next door is probably number 24"). Buffalo's disputed rows were only defensible because this was written down. **Separate what you checked from what you inferred.** "One bulletin for all four churches" is a claim. "Inferred from the merger; no bulletin read" is a different claim, and the reader needs to know which one they're looking at. Put anything you couldn't check under *Not yet confirmed*, with the step that would settle it. If it has a date ("the parish says it closes after Labor Day"), put it in `revisit_after`. A deferral with a date and a next step gets done. "Someone should look at this" doesn't. **Record what you ruled out.** If a directory still lists a building this parish no longer uses, say so in the parish's *Worship sites* and give that building its own `excluded/` record. Otherwise the next person spends an hour rediscovering it. The templates `new` writes give each kind its headings: - **parish:** *Publisher* (who publishes, which issue you read, quoted), *Worship sites* (why these churches, and what the diocese lists that is not here), *Website and bulletin provider*, *Not yet confirmed*. - **church:** *Holds Mass* (current, dated), *Name and address* (sources, agreement, coordinates). - **excluded:** *Why it is excluded* (the claim, quoted and dated), *What would change this*. - **open:** *What is known*, *Why it is not decided*. Validation treats a leftover `TODO` or an empty explanation as incomplete, and `promote` refuses until none are left. A good exclusion, from Buffalo: > **St. Thomas Aquinas, 450 Abbott Rd, Buffalo — closed, last Mass 2024-11-09.** The 13 Oct > 2024 issue of the Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin (container 14/0940) still names > it in the masthead and announces "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, > November 9th at 11:30 AM"; the 10 Nov masthead has dropped it; the 17 Nov issue says "Now > that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed". A bad one: *"Closed. Part of the Road to Renewal consolidation."* That was a plan, and in Buffalo the plan was wrong about several churches still holding Mass two years later. ## Sources Look for these for every diocese and record in `diocese.md` what you found, where it is, and how far it can be trusted there. Diocese-wide lists answer most questions in a few fetches. Buffalo went from 62% to 79% coverage in one session by reading two diocesan pages nobody had opened. | source | good for | lags on | |---|---|---| | **A current bulletin** | who publishes, which buildings have Mass, closures dated to the week | nothing, **so it wins every disagreement** | | The parish or family's own site | Mass schedule, "our churches" page (often lists closures with dates) | old domains live on after a merger | | The diocese's parish directory / finder | addresses, coordinates, homepages, often the canonical structure in the names | closures (Buffalo's listed a church **demolished in 2023** and one closed in **2008**), dead homepages | | The diocese's family/cluster list | which parishes are grouped, and their worship sites | closures; and a group is not a bulletin | | The diocese's Mass-times pages | finding places no directory lists (Buffalo found a shrine with eleven weekend Masses) | a closed church was still listed thirteen days after its last Mass | | Closed-parish / sacramental-records index | which parishes ended and where their records went | says a *corporation* ended, never that a building is shut | | Pastoral plans, closure announcements | leads for what to check | they're plans; several of Buffalo's never happened | | GCatholic | a second independent address, a Plus Code on the building, Eastern churches flagged | closures; may omit the cathedral | | ParishesOnline / eCatholic / DiscoverMass | the bulletin itself, when the parish site blocks you | account names accumulate old members | | OpenStreetMap | whether a building exists, independent coordinates | street numbers sometimes | | News, Mass Mob sites | dating a closure, reasons | whatever they don't cover | For structure, a current bulletin beats the family list, which beats the directory. The plan says what the diocese intended; the bulletin says what happened. ## Method Work in this order and only fall through when a step can't answer. Commit as you go. 1. **Set up.** `pnpm diocese init --name ... --state XX --gcatholic `. Fill in `diocese.md` *Sources* as you find each list. 2. **Get rosters.** `pnpm diocese roster fetch gcatholic`, and the diocese's own directory: `roster fetch wpsl ` if it runs WP Store Locator, otherwise scrape it with a throwaway script and `roster import directory list.json`. Import the family list and Mass-times pages the same way (`group` = the family). Rosters are what you measure against. They aren't evidence on their own, and none of them is the diocese. 3. **Read structure before researching parishes.** From the family list and the directory, sketch which parishes might share a bulletin. For each group, find its bulletin (step 4) before creating rows. It's cheaper than creating four rows and merging them later. 4. **Find each bulletin.** Two or three requests usually settle a publisher: - `pnpm diocese probe url ` shows whether the site is alive, where it redirects, whether it has been taken by a squatter, and which publication ids it embeds. - `probe po ` returns a ParishesOnline organization's address, its publication ids and its latest issues. An LPi site's `publicationWidget?id=` is the organization id, so a widget found on a parish site leads straight to its container. - `probe container 14/0434 --pages 3` walks back through the Sundays and prints the latest masthead. `--all --step 4` gives one issue a month: **read one masthead and you have a snapshot; read two and you have a changelog** of who joined and who left. - `probe pdf --grep ""` gets the text of any bulletin. Grep a family bulletin's Mass-schedule codes across monthly issues to date a closure to the week, then look for the issue that announces it. - When a parish site blocks every fetcher, DiscoverMass often serves the same PDF, one listing per church. 5. **Decide one bulletin or several.** Merge only when the family's own bulletin is current **and** each member's own old channel (container, widget, bulletin page) has gone silent, or the member says itself that it has folded in ("St. Philomena Parish is now part of the ... Family of Parishes ... Check Bulletin"). **One live member channel means no merge.** If you can't find a member's bulletin, that isn't evidence that it shares someone else's, so keep its row and say so. Record `publication` ids on every row you settle. 6. **Add churches under their publisher** with `new church --parish

--from gcatholic: --from directory:`. This prefills the address and Plus Code coordinates, links both entries, and adds them as evidence. Confirm Mass against the current bulletin or schedule before writing *Holds Mass*. 7. **Account for the rest.** `pnpm diocese coverage ` lists every roster entry that is

---
name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
city_aliases:
  Frugality: Fallentimber
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
  Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City;
  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.
- **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of
  them (ids 17xxx) are Byzantine or other Eastern Catholic churches in the territory
  (Eparchy of Passaic / Archeparchy of Pittsburgh): `other-jurisdiction`. GCatholic still lists
  churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John
  chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary,
  Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin.
- **Clergy list:** https://www.dioceseaj.org/clergy/ lists every priest with his parishes:
  the quickest way to settle which parishes share a pastor. The `/daj_parish/<slug>/` pages are
  JS-rendered and carry no pastor text; `/bishops-appointments-2/` 403s after many requests.
- **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral
  plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above.
- **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org
  (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap)
  mention no closures or mergers.

### Bulletin publishers here

Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows
otherwise.

- **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken
  (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`)
  list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is
  `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 =
  not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the
  directory lacks. A joint bulletin may sit under only one of its churches' slugs (Our Lady
  Queen of Angels, Central City carries the issue for Holy Family, Hooversville and All Saints,
  Boswell, whose own pages are empty): a no-homepage parish can be a worship site of a
  neighbour's row, so read the neighbours' mastheads before calling it `no_bulletin`. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St.
  Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a
  chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids.
- **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS,
  stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and
  stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist
  with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St.
  Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several
  church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte
  "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as
  `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church
  page, not a tokenised download link.
- **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www.<domain>/bulletins` usually opens in
  headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged.
- **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins
  (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API
  (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`)
  lists organizations near a point.
- **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly;
  `page-pdfs` on the site reads it.
- **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=<id>`, PDFs at `pdfs/<id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`):
  broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/<id>`):
  a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/
  <code>`): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive.
- **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (14/0551), St. Clement, Johnstown (14/1971, image
  pages) and St. John Vianney/Transfiguration (14/1788). tesseract is not installed: render pages
  with `pdftoppm` and read them.
- **`dated-post <bulletin page>`** reads a site with one child page per issue (St. Francis of
  Assisi, Johnstown, /bulletin-3/; unpinned `page-pdfs` picked a 2021 PDF). Empty orgs: Roaring
  Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones.
- **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph,
  Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin`
  rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an
  empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages
  (`<name>.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS
  (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo
  snippet via `visit.py` reads them.
- **A public Facebook post URL** opens in headed Chrome (`visit.py --text`) without a login, though
  the profile page doesn't: find post URLs with `ddg.sh`. Quote them as notes (`recheck` gets 400).
  ParishesOnline's "no publications" text is not found by `recheck` either: note, not quote.
- **Evidence for a `no_bulletin` church being open**: obituary snippets ("funeral Mass at
  <church>", via `tools/ddg.sh "<query>"`), alongside the directory and Discover Mass times.
  Discover Mass pages 503 and then Wordfence-block even headed Chrome after repeated hits:
  read each once.
- **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton;
  `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one.
- **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip
  and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale).
- **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works;
  curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/<any-slug>` answers 200 with a
  generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing.
- **WebParish is live for several parishes** (St. Thomas, Bedford; St. Anthony and St. Elizabeth
  Ann Seton, Windber, `PDFs MMDDYY.pdf` and `SEAS<YYYY-MM-DD>Bulletin.pdf`). A parish's own
  domain can redirect to its WebParish site (stelizabethannsetonwindber.com). For a parish with
  no directory homepage, a DuckDuckGo search (`uv run python visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..."`)
  finds these. Sister parishes with one pastor can each post a bulletin listing the same
  combined Mass rota (Windber): two rows while both channels are live.
- For St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to
  `webparish.com/aj/<name>/index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists
  `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it.
- **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18
  Oct issue was not up on 21 Oct): `newest-recent` is then expected, not a fault.
- **2MHost** (stjohneverettpa.org) uses `<base href>`; the fetch code honours it since batch 7.
- **`probe pdf` can't take a URL with spaces**: pass `%20`.
- **An iframe-embedded bulletin list** (Queen of Archangels, Clarence: Google Sites page with a
  Railway-hosted iframe `qoaa-bulletin-embed-production.up.railway.app/` listing `.../MM-DD-YYYY.pdf/raw`):
  point `page-pdfs` at the embed URL. Squarespace (Renovo) links `/s/M-D-YY.pdf` from buttons.
- **Two sites, one PDF** (Bellefonte/Spring Mills, old Buford Design sites on `http://` with bad
  certificates): equal md5s of the two sites' copies prove one bulletin. The Bellefonte copies
  answer a JavaScript reload page without a browser, so the row reads the Kateri site.
- **`dated-post`** also reads Our Lady of Victory, State College (`/bulletin-archive/<month-d-yyyy>/`).
- **Two homepages, one bulletin:** the two Cresson parishes' separate Weebly sites both point at
  one ParishesOnline org (14/1078). Follow each site's "Weekly Bulletin" link before making two rows.
- **Word bulletins** (St. Michael, Saint Michael: Weebly `/uploads/.../MM-DD-YYYY_webbulletin.docx`):
  the pipeline has no `.docx` reader, so `fetch:check` fails at download; `no_bulletin` with the
  URL pattern recorded. Franciscan-staffed parishes here (OFM Conv., TOR) often post image-only
  or Word bulletins.
- `tools/fill_record.py` appends evidence after the last evidence line even when a key such as
  `parish:` follows the list (as `new excluded --parish` writes it): move `parish:` above
  `evidence:` first.
- **Campus and shrine Masses** (Mount Aloysius College; Saint Francis University's chapel; the
  Loretto shrine's summer Sunday Mass) go to `open/` until a source says they are public.
- **One pastor, one bulletin is common in Cambria**: Fr. Nale's stjic.org bulletin carries all
  four of his parishes (Summerhill, New Germany, South Fork, Wilmore), whose own Discover Mass
  pages are empty. Directory Mass times lag the bulletin there by up to two hours.
- **Nominatim** `q=<church name>+<town>` finds church nodes where `street=` fails.
- **Nominatim** answers through the sandbox (`nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?street=..&city=..
  &state=..&format=json`, with a user agent): use it to tell which of two GCatholic points is
  the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors,
  Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968).
- **webparish.com/aj/<name>/** answers 406 (Mod_Security) to curl; headed Chrome needs the
  explicit `/index.php`. It is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi,
  Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing
  to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow
  the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home.
- **A page that links a Word calendar before its PDFs** (saintbenedictschurch.com, Carrolltown)
  makes `page-pdfs` pick the `.docx` (`not_pdf`); use the Discover Mass copy. That GoDaddy site
  fails https (certificate) and works over `http://www.`. An eCatholic homepage can point its
  Bulletins menu at Discover Mass (Nicktown): read its links with `visit.py --links`.
- **Discover Mass's daily cap** blocks raw curl before the pipeline's own fetch
  (`tools/browser_get.py`) is refused: use that to read a cover. `recheck` gets 503s there.
- **GCatholic-only entries can be open missions**: St. Joseph Mission, Carrolltown (Mass a few
  times a year, own site sjmc1830.com) is in no directory. Absence from the directory settles
  nothing.
- **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael,
  Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every
  time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works.
- **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859),
  St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare
  403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try,
  and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:<id>` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date
  files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`).
- **Wix image bulletins** (St. Anne, Davidsville): one JPEG per week on the Bulletin page,
  alt text `MMDDYYYY.jpg`; `page-images <page>` reads it (the date parser takes MMDDYYYY since
  batch 9). St. Peter, Somerset: PHP `bulletin.php` linking `site_docs/<n>.pdf`. New Baltimore:
  WordPress, posts about a week late.
- **Partner bulletins:** in Johnstown both no-homepage parishes in batch 12 (St. Patrick; St.
  Michael) are carried in their pastor's other parish's bulletin. Read the partner's cover
  first. A parish domain redirecting to the partner's site (stpatrickjtown.com → the
  cathedral; `probe url` says REDIRECT-OFFSITE) is a fold-in, not a squat.
- **Duda** (the Johnstown cathedral, `irp.cdn-website.com`) resets curl intermittently; retry.
  Its `/welcome#WeeklyBulletin` lists `files/uploaded/YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` (not always zero-padded).
  omostoday.com (WordPress/Elementor) posts scanned issues: render with `pdftoppm`.
- **Two parishes on one site** (St. Therese and St. Anne, sttheresejohnstown.com, one PDF each
  per week): recipes can't filter by file name, so each row points at a different page whose
  list puts its own PDF first (homepage vs `/bulletins/`), with `#fragment` publication ids to
  keep them distinct. Fragile: re-check both picks if the site reorders.
- **WordPress PDF Embedder** (Visitation BVM, Johnstown, found by DuckDuckGo) turns PDF links
  into canvases; `page-pdfs <site>/category/<cat>/feed/` reads the RSS feed instead.
- **Third-party Mass-time aggregators** (catholicmasstime.org, catholicchurch.directory)
  disagree with each other and the directory: never a second source.
- **An eCatholic id on a site doesn't mean the bulletin is there**: standrewjohnstown.org is
  eCatholic (36351) but its bulletin folder is empty and its Bulletins menu goes to Discover Mass.
- **Self-hosted, odd hosts:** SiteGround WordPress (mhtcc.org, Huntingdon; stbenedictchurch.org,
  Johnstown; `tools/browser_get.py <page> <pdf> <out>` downloads a PDF through Chrome) drops `probe pdf`
  and plain-http curl (RemoteDisconnected or an sgcaptcha page); use https with a Chrome user
  agent, or `visit.py --bulletin`. Homestead (scosmu.org, Mount Union) resets https; `http://www.`
  works, PDFs named `<Month>_<D>.pdf` on its About-Us page.
- **findglocal.com/US/<town>/<id>/<page>** mirrors a Facebook page's posts and Mass times
  without a login: useful evidence for `no_bulletin` parishes (Dudley).
- **College campus Masses** (Juniata College, Tussey Hall) appear in the directory's Mass
  times but in no bulletin: `open/` until someone confirms they are public.
- **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans).
  `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a
  quote, and says so.
- **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in
  the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a
  second source before verifying.
- **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/),
  Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date).
- **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona
  cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads.
  Cite that page directly.
- `tools/fill_record.py` fills evidence and body into a new record (see the tools README).
- `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them.

## Rules settled for this diocese

Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them.

- **Campus Masses** (orchestrator, 2026-10-21): a college chapel whose Mass no source calls
  public goes in `open/` (Juniata, Mount Aloysius, Saint Francis University). One a source calls
  public but that no readable bulletin lists is `excluded/` with `no-bulletin` (Penn State's
  Nittany Catholic: "ALL ARE WELCOME AT OUR LITURGIES"). Either becomes a church under a row when
  a bulletin lists it.
- **Two linked parishes with no bulletin stay two `no_bulletin` rows** (Dysart/Frugality,
  Chest Springs/Ashville, the four south Somerset parishes) until a bulletin shows one is shared.

## Log

Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.
Reusable scripts for mapping the Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown (scratch, not committed).
- `discovermass-church-urls.txt`: all 20,279 Discover Mass church page URLs (from `wp-sitemap-posts-item-1..11.xml` on discovermass.com, 2026-10-21); `grep -i <town>` finds a church's slug when `?s=` search is broken. A page's "Visit Website" link gives the parish's homepage.
- `fill_record.py <record.md> <evidence.yaml> <body.md> [key=value ...]`: replaces a freshly created record's `evidence: []` (or appends to its evidence list) with the YAML items in a file, replaces the body with a Markdown file, and sets frontmatter keys. Run with `python3 -I`. Quote any `quote:` value containing ": " yourself.
- `browser_get.py <referer-page> <file-url> <out>`: downloads a PDF with the fetch pipeline's own HTTP client (SiteGround sgcaptchas curl and `probe pdf` on stbenedictchurch.org PDFs, but not this); run with `uv run python`, then `pdftotext`.
- `ddg.sh "<search words>" [chars]`: DuckDuckGo result text and off-DDG links through headed Chrome; run from the repo root.

content.text:
Batch 23 of 24 is committed and pushed. The last batch is running now: it records GCatholic's 15 Eastern Catholic churches as outside this diocese, and settles four leftover leads. Those are a National Catholic church in Johnstown, a St. Joseph in Coupon, the Carmelite monastery in Loretto, and a reported weekday Mass in Chest Springs.

- **Batch 23:** Lock Haven, Renovo and Queen of Archangels in Clarence each have a bulletin that downloads. Saints Peter and Paul in Philipsburg has no bulletin the scout could find. Lock Haven and Renovo share a pastor but publish separate bulletins, so they stay as two rows.
- **Coverage:** every one of the 93 churches in the diocese's own directory is accounted for. GCatholic's only gaps are those 15 Eastern Catholic churches.
- **So far:** 71 parish rows. 52 have a bulletin the pipeline can read (Discover Mass 6, eCatholic 7, ParishesOnline 6, other sites 33). 19 are marked "no bulletin" and stay off the site.
- **Pastor conflict:** for two Somerset parishes, the diocese's clergy page names Fr. Michael Wolfe as pastor. New Baltimore's website names Fr. Stephen Shin, OFM Cap. Both versions are in the records. It doesn't change any rows, since neither parish has a bulletin.

19 "no bulletin" rows is a lot. After the last batch, a scout will re-search the ones checked in the early batches, before web search was turning up hidden bulletin sites. Then come the final checks and the PR.

The Altoona-Johnstown Roman Catholic Diocese said it is too early to discuss the future of St. Joseph Roman Catholic Church in Coupon because parishioners are still going through the grieving and recovery process. About 300 parishioners will begin attending Mass in the nearby social hall this weekend after a blaze ripped through their 100-year-old historic church on Sunday. And while firefighters were able to save the Eucharist, vestments, several statues and books, what remained was destroyed by fire – with the exception of the crucifix that hung over the altar. “The crucifix was untouched, and it was able to be brought out (of the church),” said Rob Egan, diocesan spokesman. “That was God’s work, there.” Egan said future discussions with Bishop Joseph Adamec, parish priest Rev. Brian Saylor and members of the parish councils will be held in a reasonable time. “I know in the interest of the parishioners, so things can move forward, discussions will begin as soon as possible,” Egan said. And much of those discussions will evolve around finances. While the church did carry diocese-funded insurance, it was only a partial policy. He said St. Joseph’s parish pastoral and finance councils made a decision in the mid-1990s not to continue the full property loss coverage insurance because of cost factors, in an effort to run the church cost-effectively to keep it open. “This parish was looked at during the consolidation discussions in 1994, and at the time, it was stated ... that if the parish could not be manned by a part-time pastor, it would probably have to be closed because of the low number of parishioners,” Egan explained. “From what I understand, that is why they stopped paying the full insurance, because if the church fell into disrepair or a disaster would happen, they couldn’t justify continuing to pay the full insurance, when they didn’t know if they could keep a pastor.” Egan said he did not immediately know the value of the structure, which would have celebrated its 100th birthday on Tuesday. He said ultimately it is up to the diocese as to whether the church will be rebuilt. “We’d basically have to fully fund the whole thing,” Egan said. “We do have insurance carriers that would help us with the immediate cost, but because we’re self-insured, it will still come out of the diocese. he and his wife, Carol, have worshipped every Sunday for more than 50 years. Word of the transfer of the Rev. Brian Saylor from St. Joseph’s to St. Rose of Lima in Altoona was delivered recently to parish members along with word that a new priest would not be named to fill the vacancy at this time. Members are being urged to attend Mass at St. Demetrius Catholic Church in Gallitzin and St. Thomas Aquinas Catholic Church, Ashville. A third option being considered by some parishioners is St. Monica Catholic Church in Chest Springs. Diocesan spokesman Tony DeGol said there has been no “formal” decision about the future of the parish, and no plans to sell the church or the rectory are in the works. “Within a year or two things may change,” he said. “We are encouraging them to attend Mass at another parish.” Weddings and funerals need to be scheduled at neighboring parishes while baptisms can be conducted by Deacon Steve Luke, temporary administrator of St. Joseph’s. Catholic education classes will continue at the church for the time being, officials said. The century-old building that long housed St. Joseph’s was destroyed by fire in September 2008. Luke and others were able to save the Eucharist, several statues, vestments and significant books from the blaze, which broke out on a Sunday shortly after Mass ended. With permission from the diocese, parish members turned out in force to renovate the parish social hall, months of work involving extensive interior work and a new roof. “It’s beautiful. They did a good job,” Carol Stasik said. “We don’t have stained-glass windows, but it’s a church.” That nod of approval for the renovation was taken by many locals as a silent sign the church, albeit a renovated social hall, would stay open for years to come. “We never believed it would close after the volunteers fixed it up,” Walter Stasik said. The decision comes down to numbers of priests available to fill the pulpits, DeGol said. The September death of Monsignor George Flinn, 69, created a vacancy at St. John Gaulbert Cathedral in Johnstown, a vacancy filled by transferring the Rev. James Crookston from St. Rose of Lima, creating the need to pull Saylor from Coupon, DeGol said. “After the fire there was a genuine effort to keep the parish alive as long as possible, but what happened (is) when Monsignor Flinn died it created a need for Father Saylor elsewhere,” DeGol said. “It’s just a case of fewer priests.” Any hope from the diocese that someday a priest may be returned to the pulpit at St. Joseph’s is like gold to Mary “Punkin” Pettenati. “We are not closed. We are still considered as St. Joseph’s Parish. We still have everything going, except we don’t have Mass,” Pettenati said. # Exploring a diocese

`data/dioceses/<diocese>/` is where a diocese the pipeline does not cover yet gets worked
out: which bulletins it publishes, which buildings hold Mass, which places were looked at
and ruled out, and the evidence for every one of those calls. `pnpm diocese promote` then
writes the rows into `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`.

The files are kept after promotion. They are the record of **why each live row is what it
is**, and that is what they are written for: someone auditing a row a year from now, human
or agent, should be able to open its file, follow the evidence, and confirm or overturn it
in a few minutes.

This guide comes out of the Diocese of Buffalo expansion (PR #14): 72 parishes and 151
churches, reworked several times. Most of its mistakes were in **structure** (which rows are
one bulletin), not coverage, and most of its time went on re-deriving things that were
never written down. The rules and the file layout below are there to avoid both.

- [The model](#the-model): what a parish row and a church row are
- [Files](#files): layout and fields
- [The explanation](#the-explanation): what to write, and what an auditor needs
- [Sources](#sources): what to look for, and how far to trust each
- [Method](#method): the order to work in, cheapest first
- [Traps](#traps): the things that produced confident wrong answers in Buffalo
- [Commands](#commands)

## The model

**One parish row = one bulletin.** A `parish` row is a bulletin publisher, because the
pipeline reads bulletins: its `website` is where that bulletin can be found, and its churches
are the worship sites the bulletin's Mass schedule covers. The diocese's own units do not
decide this:

- A *family*, *cluster* or *pastorate* of several canonical parishes that publishes one
  bulletin is **one** row with several churches.
- A family whose members each publish their own bulletin is **several** rows.
- A canonical merger does not merge rows, and a rescinded one does not split them. Buffalo
  had both: Holy Cross and Our Lady of Hope share Family #23 but are separate rows, while
  St. John and St. Mary of the Angels in Olean had their merger rescinded and still publish
  one bulletin (one row). Bulletins change too: Fourteen Holy Helpers kept its own bulletin
  after merging into Queen of Heaven, but by September 2026 it shared the Blessed Family #7
  bulletin with Queen of Heaven and St. John Vianney (one row).
- A family's size tells you nothing. Buffalo's families went every way: some single
  bulletins over four parishes, some with every member separate.

Record the grouping in `group` anyway: `audit` uses it to find rows that may be one bulletin.

**One church row = one place where Mass is celebrated publicly now.** Missions, oratories,
chapels, shrines and campus chapels count, and so does a building with Mass four times a
year. What the place is called doesn't matter; whether Mass happens there does. A building
whose parish closed can still be a worship site. In Buffalo, every closure source said
St. George (West Falls) had closed, but the family's own schedule still listed a Saturday
Mass there.

**Everything else goes in `excluded/`, with a reason** (`pnpm diocese new excluded --help`
lists them):

| reason | use it for |
|---|---|
| `closed` | no Mass any more: closed, merged away, sold, demolished. Put the date in `last_mass` when a source gives it (`2017` or `2017-06` when it gives no day) |
| `no-bulletin` | **open**, with public Mass, but nothing the pipeline could read. Don't file these under `closed`; that list has to stay a record of what actually shut down |
| `no-public-mass` | offices, schools, pregnancy centers, cemeteries, private convent or hospital chapels |
| `not-catholic` | a same-named Orthodox, Episcopal, Lutheran... church |
| `other-jurisdiction` | another diocese or an Eastern Catholic eparchy (GCatholic lists these in the territory) |
| `other` | none of the above; the explanation says what |

An exclusion states a fact about a place, so it needs a source that states it. If
everything points to closed but nothing says so, it goes in `open/`, not `excluded/`.

**Settled policy** (the data owner decided these during the Buffalo work; apply them rather
than reopening them):

1. A social-media page can be a parish `website` if the bulletin is actually posted there.
   A page that merely exists is not enough.
2. A closed church is removed from `churches.csv` (promote does this for a promoted church
   moved to `excluded/`), and its page on the site is allowed to 404. There is no `closed`
   column.
3. The dataset tracks real worship sites, not a diocesan list. A place with solid evidence
   goes in whether or not the diocese's directory lists it.
4. The site shows only places it can give a schedule for. A `no_bulletin` parish row and its
   churches stay in the records, with their evidence and a `revisit`, but `promote` leaves
   them out of the live CSVs (and removes them if they were live, which `validate` warns about
   until it is done), and they carry no `promoted` stamp. `coverage` counts their churches as
   accounted for but not in its `modelled` figure. Setting the row to a real provider when a
   bulletin turns up puts it back. (Settled 2026-10-07; until then these rows
   were kept on the map with no Mass times.) A place that was never a parish row of its own
   goes in `excluded/` with `reason: no-bulletin` as before.

## Files

```
data/dioceses/<diocese>/
  diocese.md            sources, their quirks, rules settled for this diocese, a dated log
  parishes/<slug>.md    one per bulletin publisher      -> a data/parishes.csv row
  churches/<slug>.md    one per worship site            -> a data/churches.csv row
  excluded/<slug>.md    looked at and ruled out, with a reason
  open/<slug>.md        found, not decided: what is known and what would settle it
  rosters/<name>.json   outside lists the diocese is measured against (written by tools)
```

Every record is YAML frontmatter plus a Markdown body. The slug is the file name. Edit the
files directly: create them with `pnpm diocese new ...` (which fills in the frontmatter and
an explanation template), write the explanation and evidence, and run `pnpm diocese
validate`. Use the commands for anything that touches several files: `merge`, `rename`,
`exclude`, `coverage --link`, `promote`. Those are refused, with nothing written, if they
would add a validation error.

```markdown
---
name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
website: https://cathedralsyracuse.org
bulletin_provider: parishes_online
provider_id: cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202
publication: [po-org:cathedral-of-the-immaculate-conception-13202, lpi:0018000000Qbz9eAAB, po-container:06/0091]
group: ''
evidence:
- url: https://container.parishesonline.com/bulletins/06/0091/20260920B.pdf
  seen: 2026-09-25
  quote: 'Weekend: Sat. 5:10 pm … Sun. 7:30 am, 9:45 am, 5:10 pm'
  note: Masthead of the 20 September 2026 issue, page 1. Names the cathedral alone.
---

## Publisher

The cathedral publishes its own weekly bulletin through ParishesOnline...
```

`syracuse/` is a complete worked example: a whole diocese explored in one pass by eight
parallel agents, one per region, including exclusions of every kind, parishes folded into
shared bulletins, and a canonical merger dated from the news rather than a guess.

### Fields

Every kind has `name`, `evidence`, and optionally `revisit` (the next thing to check) with
`revisit_after` (a date). `todo` lists revisits that are due.

**parish**
- `website`: where the bulletin can be found (required, unique across the dataset).
- `bulletin_provider`: `parishes_online`, `ecatholic`, `discover_mass`, `other`,
  `google_drive` or `no_bulletin` (kept in the records, left off the site: Settled policy
  4). `fetch` reads ParishesOnline and DiscoverMass by
  `provider_id` (the org slug from `parishesonline.com/organization/<slug>`, the church slug
  from `discovermass.com/church/<slug>/`). It reads eCatholic, `other` and `google_drive`
  from `website`, so for eCatholic the website has to be the eCatholic-hosted site, and for
  `google_drive` it has to link the shared folder. For `other` and `google_drive`,
  `provider_id` may pin how to read the site, as a recipe: a collector, the bulletin page,
  or both (`page-pdfs https://example.org/bulletins`). Run
  `pnpm fetch:check --diocese <d> --parish <slug>` (which reads the rows from these
  records, so it works before promotion) and record the `recipe` it prints once its pick is
  this week's bulletin (see "How the `other` resolver reads a site" in the main README).
- `publication`: ids of the bulletin itself, as `scheme:value`. **Two parish rows may never
------
---
name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown
state: PA
website: https://www.dioceseaj.org
status: exploring
gcatholic: alto0
city_aliases:
  Frugality: Fallentimber
---

Eight counties of west-central Pennsylvania: Blair (Altoona), Cambria (Johnstown, Ebensburg),
Bedford, Centre (State College), Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset. It borders Erie to
the north-west, Pittsburgh and Greensburg to the west, Harrisburg to the east, and Scranton
and Erie to the north. The diocese has no families or clusters: most parishes have one
church, and many share a pastor with one to three neighbours ("linked" parishes), which is
where shared bulletins are likely.

## Sources

Diocese-wide lists worth reading, what each is good for, and how far to trust it here.

- **Parish directory:** `rosters/directory.json`, scraped 2026-10-21 from the nine pages of
  https://www.dioceseaj.org/parishes/ (WordPress `daj_parish` and `daj_church` posts; the REST
  API answers 401). 87 parishes and 93 churches; six parishes list two churches (Holy Spirit,
  Lock Haven; Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Altoona; Our Lady Queen of Angels, Central City;
  Prince of Peace, Northern Cambria; Queen of Archangels, Clarence; Sts. Gregory and
  Barnabas, Johnstown). A single-church parish's church post has no name or address, so the
  roster entry takes the parish's. Each entry has the directory's Mass times, pastor, phone and
  (for 55 parishes) a homepage. Pastors are the best lead for shared bulletins.
- **GCatholic:** `rosters/gcatholic.json` (key `alto0`), 109 entries with Plus Codes. 15 of
  them (ids 17xxx) are Eastern Catholic churches in the territory, each `excluded/` as
  `other-jurisdiction`: 12 of the Ruthenian Metropolitanate of Pittsburgh and 3 (Johnstown,
  Northern Cambria, Revloc) of the Ukrainian Eparchy of Saint Josaphat in Parma, per each
  GCatholic page's "Jurisdiction:" line. GCatholic still lists
  churches the directory has dropped (St. Joseph, Carrolltown; St. Boniface, Hastings; St. John
  chapel, Central City; Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and St. Joseph, Portage; St. Mary,
  Meyersdale), each to be settled from a bulletin.
- **Clergy list:** https://www.dioceseaj.org/clergy/ lists every priest with his parishes:
  the quickest way to settle which parishes share a pastor. The `/daj_parish/<slug>/` pages are
  JS-rendered and carry no pastor text; `/bishops-appointments-2/` 403s after many requests.
- **Clusters / families of parishes:** none. The diocese's site has no grouping or pastoral
  plan page (sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Mass times:** only in the directory entries above.
- **Closed parishes and where their records went:** no page found on dioceseaj.org
  (page and post sitemaps checked 2026-10-21).
- **Pastoral plan / closure announcements:** none found; the news posts (36 in the sitemap)
  mention no closures or mergers.

### Bulletin publishers here

Carried over from Harrisburg, Scranton and Allentown; correct it as this diocese shows
otherwise.

- **J.S. Paluch on Discover Mass** printed half of Harrisburg. Its `?s=` search is broken
  (PHP fatal error, 2026-10-21). Its sitemaps (`discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml`)
  list every church page: grep the town there (slugs can be unguessable: St. Mary, Altoona is
  `st-mary-immaculate-conception-altoona-pa`). Probe on the bare host (200 = exists, 404 =
  not; `www.` 301s). A church page's "Visit Website" link often gives the homepage the
  directory lacks. A joint bulletin may sit under only one of its churches' slugs (Our Lady
  Queen of Angels, Central City carries the issue for Holy Family, Hooversville and All Saints,
  Boswell, whose own pages are empty): a no-homepage parish can be a worship site of a
  neighbour's row, so read the neighbours' mastheads before calling it `no_bulletin`. Many pages here say "no bulletins available" (St. Joseph, Bellwood; St.
  Matthew, Tyrone; St. Therese): not live channels. One bulletin under a parish slug and a
  chapel slug (Mount Carmel and `our-lady-of-assumption-altoona-pa`) is one row with both ids.
- **Directory homepages are often dead or stale** (sttheresealtoona.com dead DNS,
  stmatthewtyrone.org SSL failure; the live sites are sainttheresealtoona.org and
  stmatthewtyrone.com). Directory Mass times lag too (Tyrone 10:00 vs bulletin 10:30). A page can exist
  with "no bulletins available" (St. Mark and Holy Rosary, Altoona): not a live channel. St.
  Gregory, MacDonaldton's directory homepage is a Discover Mass page. One joint bulletin can appear under several
  church slugs: record every slug. Discover Mass caps downloads per IP per day (a 134-byte
  "Maximum number of files downloaded today" reply, which `fetch:check` reports as
  `not_pdf`); its text layer is often garbled, and quotes keep the garble. Cite the church
  page, not a tokenised download link.
- **eCatholic** sites sit behind Cloudflare: `https://www.<domain>/bulletins` usually opens in
  headed Chrome (parish-site-access) when the homepage is challenged.
- **LPi / ParishesOnline:** many parishes keep empty organizations, which are not fold-ins
  (all four Altoona ones checked are empty). The search API
  (`https://f2141mdwk2.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/prod/search?searchType=organization&latitude=..&longitude=..&distance=3`)
  lists organizations near a point.
- **Wix** (St. Mary, Altoona's "The Marian"): the PDF name on `filesusr.com` changes weekly;
  `page-pdfs` on the site reads it.
- **Bon Venture** (`sponsors.bonventure.net/?page=<id>`, PDFs at `pdfs/<id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf`):
  broken https chain, use `http://`. **John Patrick Publishing** (`church-bulletin.org/<id>`):
  a listing with no PDFs is not a live channel. **FATA Online** (`fataonline.com/bulletins/
  <code>`): fixed "View Current Bulletin" link plus dated archive.
- **ParishesOnline** prints St. Patrick, Newry (14/0551), St. Clement, Johnstown (14/1971, image
  pages) and St. John Vianney/Transfiguration (14/1788). tesseract is not installed: render pages
  with `pdftoppm` and read them.
- **`dated-post <bulletin page>`** reads a site with one child page per issue (St. Francis of
  Assisi, Johnstown, /bulletin-3/; unpinned `page-pdfs` picked a 2021 PDF). Empty orgs: Roaring
  Spring, Williamsburg and the four Altoona ones.
- **Small parishes with no bulletin anywhere** (St. Thomas More, Roaring Spring; St. Joseph,
  Williamsburg; Dudley; Shade Gap; all four of Fr. Wolfe's south Somerset parishes): `no_bulletin`
  rows with their Facebook pages noted (login wall in the sandbox). Discover Mass pages with an
  empty Bulletins tab and empty ParishesOnline orgs are common. Flocknote group pages
  (`<name>.flocknote.com`) are sign-up pages, not bulletins, and render their title in JS
  (evidence as a note). catholicindex.org and findglocal.com now challenge curl; a DuckDuckGo
  snippet via `visit.py` reads them.
- **A public Facebook post URL** opens in headed Chrome (`visit.py --text`) without a login, though
  the profile page doesn't: find post URLs with `ddg.sh`. Quote them as notes (`recheck` gets 400).
  ParishesOnline's "no publications" text is not found by `recheck` either: note, not quote.
- **Evidence for a `no_bulletin` church being open**: obituary snippets ("funeral Mass at
  <church>", via `tools/ddg.sh "<query>"`), alongside the directory and Discover Mass times.
  Discover Mass pages 503 and then Wordfence-block even headed Chrome after repeated hits:
  read each once.
- **Name look-alikes elsewhere:** church-bulletin.org "Saints Philip and James" is Exton;
  `parishbulletins.com/bulletins/065` is Guelph, Ontario. Check the town before using one.
- **The directory's address can be the rectory** (St. Gregory, MacDonaldton shows Sts. Philip
  and James's 247 High St, Meyersdale).
- **Web search in the sandbox:** `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..." --text` works;
  curl to DuckDuckGo or Bing returns nothing. `church-bulletin.org/<any-slug>` answers 200 with a
  generic page, so a 200 there proves nothing.
- **WebParish is live for several parishes** (St. Thomas, Bedford; St. Anthony and St. Elizabeth
  Ann Seton, Windber, `PDFs MMDDYY.pdf` and `SEAS<YYYY-MM-DD>Bulletin.pdf`). A parish's own
  domain can redirect to its WebParish site (stelizabethannsetonwindber.com). For a parish with
  no directory homepage, a DuckDuckGo search (`uv run python visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..."`)
  finds these. Sister parishes with one pastor can each post a bulletin listing the same
  combined Mass rota (Windber): two rows while both channels are live.
- For St. Thomas, Bedford: the CHURCH BULLETIN button goes to
  `webparish.com/aj/<name>/index.php?PG=upcomingevents`, which lists
  `webparish.com/pdfs/Bulletin-M-D-YYYY.pdf`; `page-pdfs` on that page reads it.
- **Weebly** (fultoncatholic.com) posts `/uploads/.../YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` and uploads late (the 18

content.content:
the building. Overpass resets the connection. GCatholic has duplicates here (Seven Dolors,
  Beans Cove is both 23816 and 148968).
- **webparish.com/aj/<name>/** answers 406 (Mod_Security) to curl; headed Chrome needs the
  explicit `/index.php`. It is an old diocesan hosting scheme (St. Clare of Assisi,
  Johnstown; GCatholic's St. Mary, Hollidaysburg). Some of its pages are now stubs pointing
  to a parish's newer site, or dead stubs with nothing (Roaring Spring, Williamsburg): follow
  the pointer before treating it as the bulletin's home.
- **A page that links a Word calendar before its PDFs** (saintbenedictschurch.com, Carrolltown)
  makes `page-pdfs` pick the `.docx` (`not_pdf`); use the Discover Mass copy. That GoDaddy site
  fails https (certificate) and works over `http://www.`. An eCatholic homepage can point its
  Bulletins menu at Discover Mass (Nicktown): read its links with `visit.py --links`.
- **Discover Mass's daily cap** blocks raw curl before the pipeline's own fetch
  (`tools/browser_get.py`) is refused: use that to read a cover. `recheck` gets 503s there.
- **GCatholic-only entries can be open missions**: St. Joseph Mission, Carrolltown (Mass a few
  times a year, own site sjmc1830.com) is in no directory. Absence from the directory settles
  nothing.
- **GoDaddy site builder** (PDFs on `img1.wsimg.com/blobby/...`; St. Mary & St. Michael,
  Hollidaysburg) resets the sandbox's connections intermittently: `probe url` may fail every
  time and `fetch:check` several times before passing. Rerun it; `curl` on the PDF blobs works.
- **eCatholic** is common here: St. Catherine, Duncansville (37641), Our Lady of Lourdes (29859),
  St. Therese (37141), St. Joseph, Bellwood (40290), St. Matthew, Tyrone (37833). Cloudflare
  403s curl and `recheck`; headed Chrome (`visit.py`) opens them, sometimes on the second try,
  and `issues.py ecatholic ecatholic:<id>` then reads the PDFs without a browser. Some date
  files by the Saturday (St. Therese: `20261017.pdf` is the 18 Oct issue; `--day sat`).
- **Wix image bulletins** (St. Anne, Davidsville): one JPEG per week on the Bulletin page,
  alt text `MMDDYYYY.jpg`; `page-images <page>` reads it (the date parser takes MMDDYYYY since
  batch 9). St. Peter, Somerset: PHP `bulletin.php` linking `site_docs/<n>.pdf`. New Baltimore:
  WordPress, posts about a week late.
- **Partner bulletins:** in Johnstown both no-homepage parishes in batch 12 (St. Patrick; St.
  Michael) are carried in their pastor's other parish's bulletin. Read the partner's cover
  first. A parish domain redirecting to the partner's site (stpatrickjtown.com → the
  cathedral; `probe url` says REDIRECT-OFFSITE) is a fold-in, not a squat.
- **Duda** (the Johnstown cathedral, `irp.cdn-website.com`) resets curl intermittently; retry.
  Its `/welcome#WeeklyBulletin` lists `files/uploaded/YYYY-MM-DD.pdf` (not always zero-padded).
  omostoday.com (WordPress/Elementor) posts scanned issues: render with `pdftoppm`.
- **Two parishes on one site** (St. Therese and St. Anne, sttheresejohnstown.com, one PDF each
  per week): recipes can't filter by file name, so each row points at a different page whose
  list puts its own PDF first (homepage vs `/bulletins/`), with `#fragment` publication ids to
  keep them distinct. Fragile: re-check both picks if the site reorders.
- **WordPress PDF Embedder** (Visitation BVM, Johnstown, found by DuckDuckGo) turns PDF links
  into canvases; `page-pdfs <site>/category/<cat>/feed/` reads the RSS feed instead.
- **Third-party Mass-time aggregators** (catholicmasstime.org, catholicchurch.directory)
  disagree with each other and the directory: never a second source.
- **An eCatholic id on a site doesn't mean the bulletin is there**: standrewjohnstown.org is
  eCatholic (36351) but its bulletin folder is empty and its Bulletins menu goes to Discover Mass.
- **Self-hosted, odd hosts:** SiteGround WordPress (mhtcc.org, Huntingdon; stbenedictchurch.org,
  Johnstown; `tools/browser_get.py <page> <pdf> <out>` downloads a PDF through Chrome) drops `probe pdf`
  and plain-http curl (RemoteDisconnected or an sgcaptcha page); use https with a Chrome user
  agent, or `visit.py --bulletin`. Homestead (scosmu.org, Mount Union) resets https; `http://www.`
  works, PDFs named `<Month>_<D>.pdf` on its About-Us page.
- **findglocal.com/US/<town>/<id>/<page>** mirrors a Facebook page's posts and Mass times
  without a login: useful evidence for `no_bulletin` parishes (Dudley).
- **College campus Masses** (Juniata College, Tussey Hall) appear in the directory's Mass
  times but in no bulletin: `open/` until someone confirms they are public.
- **Image-only bulletins** are common in the region (St. John, Lakemont's WordPress scans).
  `pdftoppm -r 100 -f 1 -l 1 -png` renders a page to read; the evidence is then a note, not a
  quote, and says so.
- **The directory's street addresses can be wrong**: St. John, Lakemont is 344 Baynton Ave in
  the directory but 309 Lotz Ave in its bulletin, its site and GCatholic. Check against a
  second source before verifying.
- **Self-hosted `page-pdfs` sites:** the cathedral (dated PDFs at altoonacathedral.org/bulletin/),
  Sacred Heart (one fixed `/bulletin/bulletin.pdf` overwritten weekly: check the issue date).
- **Both cathedrals may be missing from the GCatholic roster**: GCatholic links the Altoona
  cathedral at `gcatholic.org/churches/northamerica/2439`, outside the list the roster reads.
  Cite that page directly.
- `tools/fill_record.py` fills evidence and body into a new record (see the tools README).
- `pnpm diocese search` does not search rosters: an empty result says nothing about them.

## Rules settled for this diocese

Decisions that apply to more than one record, and who made them.

- **Campus Masses** (orchestrator, 2026-10-21): a college chapel whose Mass no source calls
  public goes in `open/` (Juniata, Mount Aloysius, Saint Francis University). One a source calls
  public but that no readable bulletin lists is `excluded/` with `no-bulletin` (Penn State's
  Nittany Catholic: "ALL ARE WELCOME AT OUR LITURGIES"). Either becomes a church under a row when
  a bulletin lists it.
- **Two linked parishes with no bulletin stay two `no_bulletin` rows** (Dysart/Frugality,
  Chest Springs/Ashville, the four south Somerset parishes) until a bulletin shows one is shared.

## Log

Newest first: date, what was done, and the `pnpm diocese coverage` numbers after it.

## Publisher

The two parishes have no separate channel, and no bulletin file at all that the pipeline
could read. Holy Rosary (900 N. Fourth St.) has no homepage in the diocese directory; the
directory gives St. Mark (416 Sixth Ave.) `churchofsaintmarks.org`, and that site is for

gives both addresses and phone numbers, and the page says "We have included Holy Rosary
Catholic Church on this website." Both churches share Fr. Nelson Javier, T.O.R. as pastor
(the page, 21 Oct 2026; the diocese directory says the same), one weekend schedule and one
list of weekly Mass intentions ("MASSES FOR THE COMING WEEK (SM) Saint Mark Church (HR) Holy
Rosary Church", mass-information page). So this is **one row**, not two. No second channel
exists for Holy Rosary: Discover Mass has a page for each church
(`st-mark-altoona-pa`, `holy-rosary-altoona-pa`) and both say no bulletins are available.

Sun 8:30 AM, weekday Masses Monday and Friday) and `holy-rosary-altoona` (Sun 11:00 AM,
weekday Masses Tuesday and Thursday). The weekly notices also mention St. Therese's youth
group, which is a different parish (`saint-therese-of-the-child-jesus-altoona` in the
directory), not a site of this one.

nothing for `fetch` to read. `website` is the St. Mark site that serves both parishes, and
`publication` is `url:` of it. If a bulletin is ever posted as PDFs, set `other` and run
`fetch:check`. Not run now, since there is no PDF.

"""`probe url` with a real browser: see a parish website the way a person does.

`pnpm diocese probe url` fetches pages without a browser, so it reports
HTTP4XX for sites behind Cloudflare (every eCatholic site, many others),
NO-PARISH-WORDS for sites built in JavaScript (Wix, Squarespace, "Redirecting..."
shells), and no publications for bulletins that sit in an iframe widget or one
click deep. This opens the page in the pipeline's own stealth browser
(pdf_extract.browser.launch_stealth_browser) with real Chrome, headed under
xvfb, and reports the same fields `probe url` does, read from the rendered page
and its iframes. Run scripts/setup_browser.sh once per sandbox first.

Cloudflare decides per request whether to challenge, and in a Claude Code sandbox
the challenge can never be solved (brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com is denied
by the egress policy), so a challenged load is simply retried with backoff.

Usage (from the repo root; re-runs itself under xvfb-run when there is no display):
  uv run python .claude/skills/parish-site-access/scripts/visit.py URL [URL ...] [options]

  --bulletin        when a page embeds no publication id, open its bulletin links
                    (up to 5) until one does, the way detect.py does; bulletin PDFs
                    with no publisher are reported as self-hosted (url:<page>)
  --follow TEXT     after loading, follow the first link whose text or href contains
                    TEXT (case-insensitive); repeat to walk deeper (single URL only)
  --text            include the visible text of the final page (--chars N, default 4000)
  --links           include the final page's links as [text, href] (--match REGEX filters)
  --screenshot PATH full-page screenshot of the final page (look at it with Read);
                    with several URLs, -0, -1, ... is added to the name
  --html PATH       save the final page's HTML, iframes included (numbered like --screenshot)
  --retries N       loads per navigation while Cloudflare challenges (default 8)

Prints JSON: {"results": [{url, verdict, status, final_url, title, loads,
publications, bulletin_links, pdf_links, ...}]}, describing the site's own page.
verdict is one of probe url's (ok, SPAM-SQUAT, REDIRECT-OFFSITE, HTTP4XX, HTTP5XX,
NO-PARISH-WORDS) judged on the rendered page, or BLOCKED (Cloudflare challenged
every load: wait a minute and retry) or ERROR (the browser could not load it,
which includes domains that don't resolve: probe url tells DEAD-DNS apart).
With --follow, the page it ends on is described under "followed", and --text,
--links, --screenshot and --html read that page.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import re
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urljoin

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
CF_TITLE = "just a moment"
# SiteGround's "Robot Challenge Screen" (/.well-known/sgcaptcha/) clears by itself
# after 5-10 s in a headed browser, then goes back to the page.
SG_TITLE = "robot challenge"
SG_PATH = "/.well-known/sgcaptcha"
# How long one load waits for a passive challenge to clear before reloading.
CF_SETTLE_MS = 5000

None of the nine rows changed provider. All stay `no_bulletin`, and I added one dated line to each record's *Not yet confirmed* section (all in data/dioceses/altoona-johnstown/parishes/).

Methods tried: DuckDuckGo (`ddg.sh`, about 17 queries per name, town, pastor and "facebook bulletin"), the Discover Mass sitemap list, the clergy page, neighbours' bulletins, and public Facebook post URLs. Facebook profile pages on www, m and mbasic all hit the login wall. The roster is `scratch/map-altoona-johnstown/tools/discovermass-church-urls.txt`. Domains I guessed for these parishes don't resolve.

- **Records:**
  - `saint-mark-holy-rosary-altoona`: unchanged. No bulletin PDF turned up. The Facebook page's mirror on findglocal (posts to 11 Oct 2026) holds no bulletin. holy-rosary.org and stmark-parish.org are other towns. Revisit 2027-01-15.
  - `saint-thomas-more-roaring-spring`: unchanged. The only public Facebook URL was a 2020 video. The clergy page shows Fr. Zeth as administrator of Roaring Spring and Newry, and Newry's bulletin doesn't carry Roaring Spring.
  - `saint-joseph-williamsburg`: unchanged. The clergy page lists only Deacon Kevin Nester as administrator (the earlier "unverified" note is now confirmed), so no neighbouring priest's bulletin is a candidate.
  - `immaculate-conception-dudley`: unchanged. The 2018 Facebook posts ("bulletin posted at www.iccdudley.com/bulletin") point to the dead domain. The clergy page shows Fr. Mark Reid as administrator, also over Dysart, Frugality and Huntingdon. Huntingdon doesn't carry Dudley, and Dysart and Frugality are themselves `no_bulletin`. The Wayback availability check hit 429, so it wasn't read.
  - `saint-mary-shade-gap`: unchanged. The parish's Facebook page (75 likes) is behind the login wall. The only public post is a June 2026 photo.
  - `saint-gregory-macdonaldton`, `saint-mary-pocahontas`, `saint-michael-salisbury`, `saints-philip-and-james-meyersdale`: unchanged. The Discover Mass list has no further slugs for these towns. church-bulletin.org `?id=144` is Exton. St. Peter, Somerset's current bulletin (site_docs/10648.pdf) has no hit for Meyersdale, Salisbury, Pocahontas, Gregory or Wolfe.
- **Merges recommended:** none.
- **Leads:**
  - The Sts. Philip and James, Meyersdale Facebook post of 26 Aug 2026 says "We welcome Fr. Michael Wolfe to our parish. Church times had to change temporarily. Mass is held at 11:30 am on Sundays." That is current Mass-time evidence for `churches/saints-philip-and-james-meyersdale` if you want to refresh its times. I didn't edit it.
  - `saint-augustine-dysart` and `saint-joan-of-arc-frugality` still have `group: Rev. Robert P. Reese`, but the clergy page now lists Fr. Mark Reid as pastor of both, and of Dudley (administrator) and Huntingdon. Their group labels are stale, and Dudley's pastor is the same man. No shared bulletin was found.
- **Learnings:**
  - A newer lookup of the clergy page (`curl` with a browser user agent; dioceseaj.org/clergy answers 200, 294 KB) pairs each parish with its pastor or administrator. It gives Reid for Dysart, Frugality, Dudley and Huntingdon, Zeth for Newry and Roaring Spring, and Nester (a deacon, no priest) for Williamsburg.
  - Facebook post URLs that DuckDuckGo surfaces for these parishes are old (2018 for Dudley, 2020 for Roaring Spring). None carried a current bulletin.
  - `church-bulletin.org/?id=<n>` 406s plain curl with a bare user agent. `pnpm diocese probe url` reads it and shows the town in the PDF path.
  - `churchbulletin.app/find-bulletin` is a JS search app with no readable static listing.
- **Validate:** `pnpm diocese validate altoona-johnstown` reports 0 errors and 0 incomplete. The one warning is not mine: excluded `our-lady-of-the-sacred-heart-portage` is closed without a `last_mass`.

Mark Reid as administrator, also over Dysart, Frugality and Huntingdon. Huntingdon doesn't carry Dudley, and Dysart and Frugality are themselves `no_bulletin`. The Wayback availability check hit 429, so it wasn't read.
  - `saint-mary-shade-gap`: unchanged. The parish's Facebook page (75 likes) is behind the login wall. The only public post is a June 2026 photo.

+Sunday noon). Two live channels, so two rows.

+bulletin's schedule lists no other place; the directory and GCatholic list this one church for the parish.

+`http://stjohneverettpa.org/gallery/Bulletin October 18 2026.pdf` (360,776 bytes), dated 2026-10-18.
+## Not yet confirmed
+Nothing open.
