input.body:
Maps the Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown (west-central Pennsylvania: Blair, Cambria, Bedford, Centre, Clinton, Fulton, Huntingdon and Somerset counties) and promotes it: **52 parish rows and 73 churches added** to `data/parishes.csv` and `data/churches.csv`, nothing removed.

## What's in `data/dioceses/altoona-johnstown/`

- **71 parish rows.** 52 have a readable bulletin: 33 `other`, 7 eCatholic, 6 Discover Mass and 6 ParishesOnline. The other 19 are `no_bulletin`: small parishes with no bulletin online, mostly Facebook-only or posting nothing; one posts only Word files. These stay in the records with a dated `revisit` and are left off the site.
- **94 churches**, including missions and chapels found in bulletins (e.g. St. Joseph Mission, Carrolltown; Snow Shoe chapel; Assumption Chapel, Altoona).
- **21 exclusions:** 15 Eastern Catholic churches (`other-jurisdiction`: 12 Ruthenian Pittsburgh, 3 Ukrainian Parma), 2 closed (Sacred Heart, Portage; St. Joseph, Coupon), 2 `no-bulletin` (Penn State's campus Mass and the Loretto Carmel; both are public, but no bulletin lists them), 1 `no-public-mass`, 1 `not-catholic` (Polish National Catholic, Johnstown).
- **5 open questions:** three campus or shrine Masses that no source calls public, St. Boniface chapel in Hastings, and the Juniata College Mass.
- **Coverage:** the diocese directory (scraped into `rosters/directory.json`, 93 churches) is 93/93 accounted for, and GCatholic is 109/109.
- **Shared bulletins** settled from mastheads. Several linked parishes publish one bulletin, among them the four Summerhill/New Germany/South Fork/Wilmore parishes, Central City/Boswell/Hooversville, and the Johnstown cathedral with St. Patrick. Others that share a pastor publish separately, such as Windber, Lock Haven/Renovo and Bellwood/Tyrone.

## Checks

- `pnpm diocese validate altoona-johnstown`: 0 errors, 0 incomplete. One warning: Sacred Heart, Portage is closed, but no source gives its last Mass date.
- `audit --fetch`: the only groups flagged are pairs of `no_bulletin` rows with one pastor, and no shared ids were found.
- Full `fetch:check`: 47 of 52 ok. The other 5 are Discover Mass rows refused by its daily download cap (134-byte replies). Each passed its own check earlier the same day; they should be re-checked once the cap resets.
- `uv run pytest`: 1192 passed. `uv run ruff check .`: clean.

## Fetch code changes (each with a test)

- `fetch._http_get` percent-encodes the `Referer` header. Huntingdon's WordPress file name contains an en dash, and sending it raw raised `UnicodeEncodeError`.
- `parish_sites.collectors.page_pdf_candidates` resolves links against the page's `<base href>`. Everett's links resolved to a 404 without it.
- `parish_sites.dates.parse_date` reads an unseparated `MMDDYYYY` (`10112026.jpg`, a Wix image bulletin in Davidsville), but only for a year next to the reference date, so eight-digit ids don't become dates.

## Lessons for every diocese

- **Discover Mass's `?s=` search is broken** (PHP fatal error). Its sitemaps `discovermass.com/wp-sitemap-posts-item-{1..11}.xml` list every church page, and grepping a town finds slugs you couldn't guess. This belongs in the README's *Traps*.
- **A no-homepage parish is often a worship site in its neighbour's or partner's bulletin**, or has a site that only a web search finds. Here that meant WebParish sites and redirecting domains. `visit.py "https://duckduckgo.com/?q=..."` is a working search from the sandbox; curl to search engines returns nothing. Check both before calling a parish `no_bulletin`.
- **Cathedrals can be missing from the GCatholic roster.** GCatholic links them at `/churches/northamerica/<id>`, outside the list `roster fetch gcatholic` reads; both cathedrals here were missing. `roster fetch` could follow the diocese page's own links.
- **Recipes can't filter by file name.** St. Anne and St. Therese, Johnstown post separate PDFs on one site, so each row relies on a different page's list order. A file-name pattern in recipes would make this robust.
- **No `.docx` reader.** St. Michael, Saint Michael posts only Word bulletins, so the row is `no_bulletin`.
- **WordPress PDF Embedder hides PDF links from page recipes**; `page-pdfs <site>/category/<cat>/feed/` reads the RSS feed instead. Equal md5s of two sites' copies prove a shared bulletin.
- **The diocese's clergy page settles who shares a pastor**, which is the best lead for shared bulletins where there are no families.

content.text: {"id":"4959743924","url":"https://github.com/project-carlo/project-carlo/pull/145"}

I've mapped the Diocese of Altoona–Johnstown, added it to the live data and opened a PR: [project-carlo/project-carlo#145](https://github.com/project-carlo/project-carlo/pull/145).

- **Parishes:** 71 bulletin rows in total. 52 have a bulletin the pipeline can read and were added to `data/parishes.csv`. The other 19 publish nothing readable online (mostly small, Facebook-only parishes; one posts Word files), so they're recorded with a recheck date and kept off the site.
- **Churches:** 94 places with Mass were found; the 73 under the 52 readable rows were added to `data/churches.csv`. Nothing was removed.
- **Ruled out:** 21 places, each with its reason written down. 15 are Eastern Catholic churches belonging to other dioceses, 2 are closed, and 1 is Polish National Catholic.
- **Open questions:** 5 places are recorded but not decided, mostly college and shrine Masses that no source calls public.
- **Coverage:** every church in the diocese's own directory (93) and on GCatholic (109) is accounted for.
- **Checks:** validation shows no errors and all tests and lint pass. 47 of the 52 bulletins downloaded in the final check. The other 5 are on Discover Mass, which was refusing downloads after hitting its daily limit. Each of those passed earlier the same day, so they should be rechecked once the limit resets.
- **Fetcher fixes:** I also fixed three bugs in the bulletin downloader, each with a test. A dash character in a file name crashed it. It ignored a page's `<base href>` tag, so one site's links pointed to the wrong place. And it couldn't read dates like `10112026.jpg`.

A few calls are judgement calls worth a look in review:
- **Linked parishes:** many share a pastor. Where a bulletin shows they publish one together, they're a single row; where it doesn't, they stay separate.
- **St. Anne and St. Therese, Johnstown:** they post separate bulletins on one website. Each row depends on its own bulletin being listed first on a different page, so it would break if the site is reorganised.
- **Pastor conflict:** for two Somerset parishes, the diocese's clergy page and a neighbouring parish's site name different pastors. Both are written in the records.
- **One warning remains:** Sacred Heart in Portage is closed, but no source gives its last Mass date.

The PR description also lists improvements that would make the next diocese cheaper. The two biggest are a Word-document reader and a way to choose a bulletin by file name. If you'd like, I can watch the PR and respond to CI failures or review comments as they come in.
